# Serenity BDD

> Serenity BDD is an open-source Java library for writing acceptance and regression tests (web, REST and mobile) that produce rich living-documentation reports. Current release described here: 5.4.1 (the Playwright modules are published up to 5.3.11). Requires Java 17+. Source: https://github.com/serenity-bdd/serenity-core

## Notes for AI coding assistants

Serenity supports several styles. All of them are current and valid; none is preferred or deprecated:

- Page Objects with a step library (`@Steps`), using Selenium or Playwright
- Screenplay, using Selenium, Playwright or REST
- JUnit 5 or Cucumber as the test runner

If the user hasn't said which style to use and the project doesn't show one (check `pom.xml` for `serenity-screenplay*`, `serenity-playwright`, `serenity-cucumber`, and look at existing tests), ask. Don't pick a default. Within a project, stay in one style, one driver and one runner. Don't mix Page Objects and Screenplay in one test.

Packages that are often guessed wrongly (verified against 5.4.1):

- `@Step`, `@Steps`, `@Managed`, `@DefaultUrl`, `@WithTag`: `net.serenitybdd.annotations` (not `net.thucydides.core.annotations`).
- JUnit 5: `@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)` from `net.serenitybdd.junit5`. Don't use `@RunWith(SerenityRunner.class)` in a JUnit 5 project.
- Page Objects: `net.serenitybdd.core.pages.PageObject` and `WebElementFacade`. `PageObject.open()` is final: don't redeclare it; use `@DefaultUrl` or `openAt(url)`.
- Screenplay core: `Actor`, `Task`, `Question`, `Performable` in `net.serenitybdd.screenplay`; `OnStage` and `OnlineCast` in `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actors`; `GivenWhenThen.seeThat` in `net.serenitybdd.screenplay`.
- Screenplay with Selenium (`serenity-screenplay-webdriver`): `BrowseTheWeb` in `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.abilities`; `Open`, `Click`, `Enter`, `Hit` in `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actions`; `Target` in `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.targets` (`locatedBy` takes a String that is read as XPath if it compiles as XPath, otherwise CSS: `.new-todo` is CSS but `input.new-todo` is read as XPath and finds nothing, so use `located(By.cssSelector(..))` for tag-prefixed CSS); questions such as `Text` and `Value` in `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.questions`. `Text.ofEach(..)` is a `Question<Collection<String>>`. Web `Ensure` is `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.ensure.Ensure` (artifact `serenity-ensure`).
- Screenplay with Playwright (`serenity-screenplay-playwright`): everything is under `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright` (`abilities.BrowseTheWebWithPlaywright`, `actors.PlaywrightCast`, `interactions.*`, `questions.*`, `assertions.Ensure`). Locators are Playwright selector strings. `Text.ofEach(..)` returns `List<String>`.
- Screenplay REST (`serenity-screenplay-rest`): `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.rest.abilities.CallAnApi`, `...rest.interactions.{Get,Post,Ensure}`, `...rest.questions.LastResponse`.
- Playwright Page Objects (`serenity-playwright`): plain classes holding a `com.microsoft.playwright.Page`, registered with `PlaywrightSerenity.registerPage(page)` from `net.serenitybdd.playwright`. They don't extend `PageObject`.
- `ScenarioSteps` (`net.thucydides.core.steps`) and `Pages` (`net.thucydides.core.pages`) are correctly in `net.thucydides`. Many `net.thucydides` packages are current core packages, so don't treat that prefix as a sign of old code.
- Cucumber with JUnit 5: a `@Suite` class with `@IncludeEngines("cucumber")` and the plugin `net.serenitybdd.cucumber.core.plugin.SerenityReporterParallel`.
- Serenity 5.4.1 depends on JUnit 6.1.3 and Cucumber 8.0.4. Don't pin older JUnit or Cucumber versions in the pom: the code compiles but the tests fail at run time with "conflicting versions". Import the JUnit BOM (`org.junit:junit-bom`) to keep all JUnit artifacts aligned.
- Configuration lives in `src/test/resources/serenity.conf`. `serenity.*` and `thucydides.*` keys are synonyms. Use only keys listed in the reference.

Every page below is also available as plain markdown (the same address with `.md` appended, and all of them in one file at https://serenity-bdd.github.io/llms-full.txt). Start with the guide to writing tests, then read the page for the style in use.

- How to write and check Serenity tests with an AI assistant (request, compile, run, can it fail, read the report): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_writing_tests.md
- Using Serenity with AI assistants (AGENTS.md files, agent skill, reviewer agent, what was measured): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_using_assistants.md
- Screenplay (Selenium, Playwright, REST, Cucumber): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_screenplay_idioms.md
- Page Objects (Selenium, Playwright): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_page_object_idioms.md
- REST with SerenityRest and a step library: https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_rest_step_library.md
- Cucumber (runner, tags under Maven and Gradle, hooks, shared state, re-running failures, parallel): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_cucumber.md
- Configuration (serenity.conf, properties, environments, reading values; which source wins): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_configuration.md
- Living documentation (how titles, wording and structure become the report): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_living_documentation.md
- Reviewing tests and the report (checklist): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_review_checklist.md
- Upgrading from Serenity 2.x, 3.x or 4.x, and recognising old code (what moved, what to change; tested on real projects): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_upgrading.md
- Reading test results from files, also after a failed build (JSON outcome files, script, JSON summary): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_test_results.md
- Dependencies and configuration: https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_project_setup.md
- Troubleshooting by error message (build, report and browser problems, each reproduced and fixed): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_troubleshooting.md

Check that generated code compiles (`mvn test-compile`) before running it. Then run `mvn verify`, check that the test fails when the behaviour is broken, and read the report in `target/site/serenity/index.html`.

# Using Serenity BDD with AI Coding Assistants

AI coding assistants write Serenity tests quickly, and they most often go wrong by guessing: a package name from an old release, a method that does not exist, or a mix of two ways of working. Everything on this page is there to stop that. All of it describes the current release (Serenity 5.4.1; the Playwright modules are published up to 5.3.11), and every claim in it was checked against the released jars or by running it.

Serenity supports several ways of writing tests, and all of them are current: Page Objects with step libraries, Screenplay, Cucumber (with Screenplay or with page objects), REST with a step library or with Screenplay, with Selenium or Playwright, with JUnit 5 or Cucumber. None is recommended over another. An assistant that has these materials asks which one you want when it cannot tell from the project, instead of choosing for you.

## What is available

| Material | What it is | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Documentation pages | Exact packages, dependencies, idioms and compiling examples for each style, plus configuration, upgrading, living documentation and troubleshooting by symptom | [Idioms and Imports by Style](ai_idioms_overview) |
| Machine-readable results | The JSON outcome files Serenity writes for every test (also after a failed build), a script that summarises a run, and the optional JSON summary report | [Reading Test Results Without the HTML Report](ai_test_results) |
| `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` | An index of the documentation for AI assistants (this section first), and the full text of the pages. Every page is also plain markdown at its own address with `.md` appended, for example `https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_writing_tests.md` | [llms.txt](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/llms.txt), [llms-full.txt](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/llms-full.txt) |
| `AGENTS.md` files | One per style. They record the style, driver and runner your project uses, so an assistant stays in it | [`docs/ai/agents-md/variants`](https://github.com/serenity-bdd/serenity-core/tree/main/docs/ai/agents-md/variants) in the serenity-core repository |
| An agent skill (Claude Code) | The same material as the pages, loaded when you ask for Serenity tests: it chooses the style (or asks), writes the tests, compiles them, and reviews the report | [`docs/ai/skill/serenity-bdd`](https://github.com/serenity-bdd/serenity-core/tree/main/docs/ai/skill/serenity-bdd) |
| A test-review agent (Claude Code) | A read-only agent that judges the new tests and the report they produce: intent, business wording, grouping | [`docs/ai/skill/agents`](https://github.com/serenity-bdd/serenity-core/tree/main/docs/ai/skill/agents) |

## Installing

**Tell your assistant about the pages.** The simplest step needs no installation: give it the address of [llms.txt](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/llms.txt), or the page for your style, and ask it to compile what it writes (`mvn test-compile`).

**Add an `AGENTS.md`.** Copy the file for your style from the variants folder to the root of your project and name it `AGENTS.md`. The names are:

| File | Style |
|---|---|
| `AGENTS.po-selenium.md`, `AGENTS.po-playwright.md` | Page Objects with a step library (Selenium, Playwright) |
| `AGENTS.sp-selenium.md`, `AGENTS.sp-playwright.md`, `AGENTS.sp-rest.md` | Screenplay (Selenium, Playwright, REST) |
| `AGENTS.cuke-sp.md`, `AGENTS.cuke-pages.md` | Cucumber with Screenplay, Cucumber with page objects |
| `AGENTS.rest-steps.md` | REST with a `SerenityRest` step library |

Assistants that read `AGENTS.md` pick it up automatically. Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`, so copy the same file to `CLAUDE.md` as well.

**Install the skill (Claude Code).** Copy the folder `docs/ai/skill/serenity-bdd` from the serenity-core repository to `.claude/skills/serenity-bdd` in your project, or to `~/.claude/skills/serenity-bdd` to have it in every project. To add the reviewer, copy `docs/ai/skill/agents/serenity-test-reviewer.md` to `.claude/agents/` (or `~/.claude/agents/`). The skill loads when you ask for Serenity tests. If your project does not show which style it uses and you did not say, it asks you before writing anything.

## What was measured

Models were given test-writing tasks against a small online bookshop with known, planted defects. A generated test counted as good only if it compiled, passed on the healthy application, and failed when the application had the defect it was meant to catch. Each figure below is for three Claude models, with and without the material.

| Test | Without | With the references |
|---|---|---|
| 14 new tasks, Page Objects and Screenplay, one-shot | 62% | 81% |
| 8 new Playwright tasks, one-shot | 67% | 96% |
| 8 new REST and Cucumber tasks (written after the guidance), one-shot | 36% | 99% |
| Same tasks with tools (the model can run Maven and fix its own errors) | at or near 100% | at or near 100%, with about half as many Maven runs |

So the main gain is in code written in one go, and in fewer retries when the model can run the build. The materials were also scored for how well the generated tests work as living documentation (clear scenario titles in business language, tests grouped by function): the score went from about 70% to about 90%.

These are results from one evaluation, run by the authors of the materials, on Claude models and Claude Code. The full method and results are in the [evaluation write-up](https://github.com/serenity-bdd/serenity-core/blob/main/docs/ai/baseline-results.md) in the serenity-core repository, including what was not tested.

## Known limits

- The pages and the skill are verified against Serenity 5.4.1. Behaviour fixed in later releases is noted where it matters.
- The skill and reviewer agent are for Claude Code. The pages, `llms.txt` and the `AGENTS.md` files are plain text and work with any assistant, but they were only measured with Claude models.
- Mobile testing, Spring and Guice object factories, and cloud grid configuration are not covered.
- If a page here is wrong, or an error message you hit is missing from [troubleshooting](ai_troubleshooting), please open an issue.

# Writing Serenity BDD Tests with an AI Assistant

This page is a workflow for getting good Serenity tests from an AI coding assistant, and for checking them. It works with any assistant. Where it mentions the agent skill, that is the Claude Code skill described in [Using Serenity BDD with AI Coding Assistants](ai_using_assistants).

The short version: **say which style you want, make the assistant compile and run what it writes, and read the report yourself.** An assistant that has not been told the style will pick one, and a test that compiles and passes can still check the wrong thing.

## 1. Set up once

Do whichever of these you can; each helps on its own.

- Put an `AGENTS.md` for your style in the project root (and a copy named `CLAUDE.md` for Claude Code). It records the style, driver and runner, so every later request stays in them. See [Installing](ai_using_assistants#installing).
- Or install the agent skill, or point the assistant at [llms.txt](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/llms.txt) or at the page for your style under [Idioms and Imports by Style](ai_idioms_overview).
- Make sure the project already builds and has a working Serenity setup ([Project Setup](ai_project_setup)). An assistant extends a working project far better than it creates one from nothing.

## 2. Write the request

A good request names five things. If one is missing, a well-configured assistant asks you; a poorly configured one guesses.

| Say | Why | Example |
|---|---|---|
| The style | Serenity supports several, all current; the assistant must not mix them | "Serenity Screenplay", "Page Objects with a step library", "Cucumber with page objects" |
| The driver | Selenium and Playwright use different packages and assertions | "with Selenium", "with Playwright", "REST only" |
| The runner | JUnit 5 and Cucumber are set up differently | "JUnit 5", "Cucumber on the JUnit Platform" |
| The behaviour, in business terms | The scenario title and step wording become the report | "a reader signs in with a wrong password and sees 'Invalid email or password'" |
| The expected values, exactly | The assertion should check the specific value, not that something is shown | "the total is $80.75", "an order number of the form ORD- followed by digits" |

Also useful: how the application is found (base URL, how to start it), the accounts or test data to use, and anything it must not touch.

If you are not sure which style to choose, say so. The skill and the `AGENTS.md` files are written to make the assistant list the options and ask, not to choose for you.

## 3. Make it compile and run

Ask the assistant to run the build itself and fix what fails:

```
mvn test-compile        # catches wrong package names and methods quickly
mvn verify              # runs the tests and builds the report
```

Add `-Dheadless.mode=true` to run a browser test without opening a window. Compile errors from wrong imports are the most common fault in generated Serenity code, and the second pass fixes them. An assistant that can run Maven usually gets there; one that cannot (a chat window) will often need you to paste back the error.

If the build fails, there is no HTML report, but the result of every test is still in `target/site/serenity/*.json`; ask the assistant to read it (see [Reading Test Results Without the HTML Report](ai_test_results)). Do not stop at "it compiles". A test that passes on the application as it is has proved little until you know it can fail.

## 4. Check that the test can fail

Break the application on purpose, or point the test at a state where the behaviour is wrong, and run it again. If it still passes, it is not checking what you asked for. This is the check the evaluation used: a generated test counted as good only if it passed on the healthy application and failed on the application with the matching defect.

Common causes of a test that cannot fail:

- the assertion is on a page title or heading that is present either way;
- it checks that an element exists, not what it says;
- it asserts the right value against the wrong element;
- it waits with a sleep and checks nothing afterwards.

## 5. Read the report

Open `target/site/serenity/index.html` after `mvn verify`. Read it as someone who has not seen the code:

- Do the scenario titles say what the business behaviour is?
- Do the step names read as a story ("Reader adds 'Clean Code' to the basket"), with no selectors, ids, URLs or status codes?
- Are the tests grouped by function (packages, or `@Narrative` and readme files), so the requirements view has a sensible shape?
- Does each test end with the expectation you asked for?

The [review checklist](ai_review_checklist) has the full list, and [Living Documentation](ai_living_documentation) explains how titles and structure become the report. In Claude Code, the test-review agent applies the same checklist to the new tests and the report.

## 6. Ask for changes, one at a time

When something is wrong, say what you saw in the report and what you want instead ("the step says `Click.on(#add)`; it should say what the reader does"). Keep to one style and one driver as you iterate.

## A worked example

This is a real run, not a mock-up. Claude Opus was asked, through Claude Code with the skill installed, to write a test against a small online bookshop that the authors keep for evaluation. The application has a catalog, a basket and a checkout. The prompt (shortened here) named the style, the driver and the runner, the behaviour, and the exact expected value:

> Using Serenity BDD Screenplay with Selenium and JUnit 5, write a test where a reader signs in, adds The Pragmatic Programmer, checks out as Ada Lovelace at '1 Main St' in Germany with the terms accepted, and checks that the confirmation shows an order number of the form ORD- followed by digits.

It was also given a description of the pages (element ids and labels), as you would give for your own application.

The assistant wrote the test and its tasks, ran `mvn verify -Dheadless.mode=true`, and reported one test, no failures. The test:

```java
@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)
class PlaceOrderTest {

    @Managed(driver = "chrome")
    WebDriver browser;

    @BeforeEach
    void setTheStage() {
        OnStage.setTheStage(new OnlineCast());
    }

    @Test
    void readerCanOrderABookAndSeeTheOrderNumber() {
        Actor reader = OnStage.theActorCalled("Reader");

        reader.attemptsTo(
                SignIn.withCredentials("reader@example.com", "correct-horse"),
                AddToBasket.theBook("The Pragmatic Programmer"),
                Checkout.as("Ada Lovelace", "1 Main St", "Germany"),
                WaitUntil.the(CheckoutPage.CONFIRMATION, isVisible()));

        reader.should(seeThat("the order confirmation",
                Text.of(CheckoutPage.CONFIRMATION), matchesPattern(".*\\bORD-\\d+\\b.*")));
    }
}
```

and one of the tasks it created, with the business wording in the step title:

```java
public class AddToBasket {
    public static Performable theBook(String title) {
        return Task.where("{0} adds '" + title + "' to the basket",
                Click.on(CatalogPage.ADD_TO_BASKET_FOR.of(title)));
    }
}
```

**Step 4, can it fail?** The evaluation then ran the same test against a copy of the bookshop in which the confirmation no longer contains an order number. The test failed, with the message `Expected: an element containing 'ORD-' but: ... [Thank you! Order]`. So the assertion does check the order number, and the test was counted as good.

**Step 5, a review.** Things a reader would still want to change: the sign-in task opens a hard-coded `http://localhost:8765/login`, which belongs in `webdriver.base.url` in `serenity.conf` (see [Configuration](ai_configuration)); and the scenario title is a method name, `readerCanOrderABookAndSeeTheOrderNumber`, which the report turns into a readable title, but you may prefer a more specific one. These are the kind of follow-ups to ask for in step 6. Passing the evaluation did not mean there was nothing to improve.

## What to expect

In the evaluation (Claude models, a small test application; full figures on [Using Serenity BDD with AI Coding Assistants](ai_using_assistants#what-was-measured)):

- Written in one go, without the reference pages, a large share of tests failed: usually an import that does not exist, or a method from a different style. With the pages or the skill, most compiled and passed.
- With tools, so the assistant can run Maven and fix its own errors, nearly every test ended up good with or without the materials. What the materials changed was the number of Maven runs, about half.
- Passing is not the same as good: the checks above (can it fail, does the report read well) are still yours to do.

## Common mistakes to watch for

| In the generated code | What it means |
|---|---|
| Imports from `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.*` in a Page Objects project, or `@Steps` in a Screenplay project | Two styles mixed; ask for one |
| `Thread.sleep(...)` | A fixed wait; Serenity waits for elements itself, or use `WaitUntil` (Screenplay) |
| Selectors, ids or URLs in step titles | The report will read as a script, not a story |
| A selector like `$("button")` or `Target.the("x").locatedBy("input.x")` | A string that starts with a tag name is read as XPath, not CSS, so the element is not found at run time. Use `#id`, `.class` or `By.cssSelector(...)`; see [Page Objects](ai_page_object_idioms) and [Screenplay](ai_screenplay_idioms) |
| A numeric REST assertion like `equalTo(90.0)` that fails | REST-assured returns JSON decimals as `Float`; see [REST](ai_rest_step_library) |
| `@Managed WebDriver` in a step library or other helper class | It is filled in only in the test class, so the field is null elsewhere; extend `UIInteractionSteps` and use `getDriver()`, or use a page object. See [Troubleshooting](ai_troubleshooting) |
| A Cucumber step that is undefined or shown as pending | The step definition does not match the step text, and an undefined step fails the build; check the Cucumber expression. See [Cucumber](ai_cucumber) |
| An import such as `net.thucydides.core.annotations.Step` that does not compile | The annotations moved to `net.serenitybdd.annotations`; see [Upgrading](ai_upgrading). Many other `net.thucydides` packages are still current core packages, so judge each import against the pages |

The [troubleshooting page](ai_troubleshooting) lists build, report and browser errors by the message you see, with a fix that was reproduced.

# Idioms and Imports by Style

These pages list the exact packages, dependencies and idioms for each supported way of writing tests with Serenity BDD, with compiling examples. They are written for people and for AI coding assistants, which most often go wrong by guessing a package name.

Serenity supports several styles. All of them are current and valid:

| Approach | Drivers | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Page Objects with a step library | Selenium, Playwright | [Page Objects: Imports and Idioms](ai_page_object_idioms) |
| Screenplay | Selenium, Playwright, REST | [Screenplay: Imports and Idioms](ai_screenplay_idioms) |
| Cucumber with Screenplay | Selenium | [Screenplay: Imports and Idioms](ai_screenplay_idioms) |
| Cucumber with page objects and a step library | Selenium | [Cucumber](ai_cucumber) |
| REST with a step library (no Screenplay) | REST-assured via SerenityRest | [REST with SerenityRest and a Step Library](ai_rest_step_library) |

Use JUnit 5 as the runner for all of them. Dependencies, the report plugin and `serenity.conf` are on [Project Setup](ai_project_setup).

## Choosing a style

Pick the style the project already uses, and stay in it: one approach, one driver and one runner per project, and don't mix Page Objects and Screenplay in one test. To see which a project uses, look at `pom.xml` (`serenity-screenplay*`, `serenity-playwright`, `serenity-cucumber`) and the existing tests. For a new project, choose by what suits the team. None of the styles is deprecated.

## If you use an AI coding assistant

See [Using Serenity BDD with AI Coding Assistants](ai_using_assistants) and [Writing Serenity BDD Tests with an AI Assistant](ai_writing_tests) for the `AGENTS.md` files, the agent skill and `llms.txt`. In short: tell it which style, driver and runner you want, or point it at these pages (or at [llms.txt](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/llms.txt)). Ask it to compile its output (`mvn test-compile`) before running it. Many `net.thucydides` packages are current core packages, so that prefix on its own is not a sign of outdated code: judge each class against these pages.

# Living Documentation: Intent, Wording and Structure

Verified against Serenity **5.4.1**. The behaviour described here was run against the example at the end of the page.

## The idea

A Serenity report is read by people who will never open the code: product owners, analysts, new team members, auditors. Its Requirements tab is a description of what the application does, built from the tests. So every scenario has two jobs: check the application, and tell a reader **what the business expects and why it matters**. A test that only passes is half done.

Write for that reader:

- The **scenario title** says the business rule or outcome, as a sentence a user would recognise.
- The **steps** read as a story in business language: who does what, in what situation, and what they should see.
- The **tests are grouped by what the application does** (ordering, searching, signing in), so the report is a navigable table of contents.

## 1. Scenario titles: the rule, not the mechanics

| Poor | Good |
|---|---|
| `testCheckout1` | `A reader sees an order number after paying` |
| `loginTest` | `Signing in with a wrong password is refused with a clear message` |
| `shouldReturn201` | `Placing an order confirms it with an order number` |
| `searchTest` | `Searching by title finds only matching books` |

- **JUnit 5:** use `@DisplayName("...")` on the method; the report title is exactly that (verified). Without it, Serenity turns the method name into words (`shouldKeepEveryBookAddedToTheBasket` becomes "Should keep every book added to the basket"), so a method name written as a sentence is also fine. A `test` prefix or a number is not.
- **Cucumber:** the `Scenario:` name is the title; write it as a sentence. Say the rule being shown, not the clicks.
- Name what the user gets or what the rule is. Avoid HTTP codes, element ids, class names and the word "test" in titles.

## 2. Steps: business language, one level above the mechanics

The report lists the steps of each scenario. Make them read like the scenario narrated.

- **Screenplay:** give every `Task` a sentence with `{0}` for the actor, and put the important data in it (verified):

  ```java
  Task.where("{0} adds '" + title + "' to the basket", ...)
  // report: Ada adds 'Refactoring' to the basket
  ```

  Tasks are business actions (`SignIn.withCredentials`, `Checkout.as`). Interactions (`Click`, `Enter`) stay inside tasks, so the report shows the business level first. Questions and `seeThat` checks read as expectations: `seeThat("the order confirmation", TheConfirmation.text(), containsString("ORD-"))`.
- **Page Objects:** annotate step-library methods with `@Step("Search the catalog for '{0}'")` (verified; `{0}` is the first parameter). Put the business verb in the step method (`shopper.searchesFor(term)`), not in the test (`driver.findElement(..)`).
- **Cucumber:** the Gherkin is the documentation. Use Given/When/Then for context, action, outcome. Keep each step about the business ("When Ada places the order"), not the UI ("When I click the button with id place-order"). Use a `Background` for context shared by all scenarios, and a `Scenario Outline` with an `Examples` table for the same rule over several values, with a meaningful column per input.
- Do not put CSS selectors, XPath, URLs, element ids, sleeps or HTTP status codes in step text. They belong inside the page object, task or step definition.
- Serenity writes the lines under a task itself: `Open.url(..)` shows as "opens the browser at http://..." and `Enter`/`Click` show the element names. You can't remove them, so keep URLs in one place and give `Target`s business names (`Target.the("email field")`). The task line above them is what the reader reads first.
- The last step of a scenario states the business expectation ("the confirmation shows an order number"), not a technical detail.

## 3. Organise by function

The report's Requirements tab is a tree. Serenity builds it from how you organise the tests:

| Style | How the tree is built | Verified result |
|---|---|---|
| JUnit 5 (any style), no annotations | the **package** path of the test class | `shop.ordering.WhenAReaderBuildsABasketTest` gives `Shop (capability)` > `Ordering (feature)` > `When a reader builds a basket test (feature)` |
| JUnit 5, annotations (recent releases; see the "Annotation-Based Requirements" docs page) | `@Epic` > `@Feature` > `@Story` on the test class | `@Epic("Buying books") @Feature("Paying for an order") @Story("Pay by card")` gives `Buying books (capability)` > `Paying for an order (feature)` > `Pay by card (story)` |
| Cucumber | the **folders** under `src/test/resources/features`, and the feature file | `features/shopping/basket.feature` gives `Shopping (capability)` > `Shopping basket (feature)` |

Rules that follow:

1. **Group by capability, then feature.** For example `ordering`, `browsing`, `accounts` as packages (or folders), with one test class (or feature file) per feature inside, each holding the scenarios of that feature. Not one class called `ShopTest` with everything in it, and not one package per technical layer.
2. **Prefer one way for the whole project.** If package-based and annotated classes are mixed, the Requirements page shows both as separate top-level trees side by side (verified), and each class is found in only one of them, so the project reads as two organisations. Follow what is already there.
3. **Class names end up in the tree.** With packages, the class name becomes the feature name, `Test` suffix included (`WhenSearchingTheCatalogTest` is shown as "When searching the catalog test", seen in a real report). Put `@DisplayName("Searching the catalog")` on the class: the feature then shows that text (verified). With annotations, the `@Feature` and `@Story` text is what the reader sees. Write these as business phrases.
4. **Cucumber:** one feature file per feature, in a folder per capability; the text under `Feature:` (a paragraph of business context before the first scenario) is shown on the feature page (verified).

## 4. Descriptions of the areas

- **Cucumber:** a `readme.md` in a features folder is the description of that capability. Its first line should be the name (`## Shopping`). Verified: it appears in the report.
- **JUnit 5:** put `readme.md` files under `src/test/resources/stories/<package path>/` (for the example `src/test/resources/stories/shop/ordering/readme.md`); the text appears in the report. The same file in `src/test/resources/shop/ordering/` was **ignored** (verified).
- **`@Narrative(text = {...})` did not appear in the JUnit 5 report** in 5.4.1 (verified, both on the class and in `package-info.java`). Don't rely on it; use the `readme.md` files.

Keep a description to a few sentences: what the area is for, and the rules that matter.

## 5. What a good scenario looks like

The shape only: `SignIn`, `Checkout`, `shopper` and the rest are the project's own classes.

Page Objects + step library:

```java
@Test
@DisplayName("Searching by title finds only matching books")
void searchingByTitle() {
    shopper.searchesFor("Refactoring");
    shopper.shouldSeeOnlyBooksCalled("Refactoring");
}
```

Screenplay:

```java
@Test
@DisplayName("A reader sees an order number after paying")
void orderNumber() {
    ada.attemptsTo(
        SignIn.withCredentials(reader),
        AddToBasket.theBook("The Pragmatic Programmer"),
        Checkout.as("Ada Lovelace").inCountry("Germany"));
    ada.should(seeThat("the order confirmation", TheConfirmation.text(), matchesPattern("Thank you! Order ORD-\\d+")));
}
```

Cucumber:

```gherkin
Feature: Placing an order

  Readers pay for the books in their basket and get an order number back.

  Scenario: A reader sees an order number after paying
    Given Ada has "The Pragmatic Programmer" in her basket
    When she checks out and accepts the terms
    Then she sees an order number like ORD-1001
```

## 6. Checking it

After the tests run, the report is what the reader sees. Run `scripts/outline.py <project>/target/site/serenity` (from the skill directory): it prints the requirements tree, the scenario titles and the steps of each scenario, and flags the mechanical problems (titles that look like method names, selectors or ids in step text, ungrouped tests). Read its output as the reader would: could someone who has never seen the code say what the application does? The `serenity-test-reviewer` agent does this check and the judgement part (`review-checklist.md`).

## 7. Not covered

Pending and manual scenarios, tags and `@WithTag`, Serenity's custom requirement types (`serenity.requirement.types`), the Jira requirements provider, `@Title`, and the exact look of the HTML report.

## Examples

These files compile against Serenity 5.4.1 (Playwright examples: 5.3.11).

### `scripts/outline.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the living documentation of a Serenity run the way a reader sees it, and flag mechanical problems.

usage: outline.py <serenity report dir> [--json]
  (the directory is normally <project>/target/site/serenity; only the *.json outcome files are read)

Prints: the requirements path of each test, its title, and its steps. Then a list of FLAGS for things a reader
would trip on. The flags are objective checks; whether the wording is good is for the reviewer to judge.
"""
import glob, json, os, re, sys

SELECTOR = re.compile(r"(#[\w-]+|\.[a-z][\w-]+\b.*[>\[]|//\w|\[@|By\.\w+|css=|xpath|data-testid|getByRole|\bid=)", re.I)
URL = re.compile(r"https?://|localhost|:\d{4}\b")
HTTP = re.compile(r"\b(?:status(?: code)?|HTTP)\s*[:=]?\s*[1-5]\d\d\b|\b(?:200|201|204|400|401|403|404|422|500)\b")
PLUMBING = re.compile(r"\b(sleep|wait(?:s)? \d|findElement|executeScript|sendKeys|driver\.|click(?:s)? (?:on )?(?:the )?(?:element|button with|link with)|locator)\b", re.I)


def load(d):
    rows = []
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(d, "*.json"))):
        try:
            j = json.load(open(f))
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if not isinstance(j, dict) or "userStory" not in j:
            continue
        steps = []

        def walk(nodes, depth):
            for s in nodes or []:
                steps.append((depth, s.get("description", "")))
                walk(s.get("children"), depth + 1)
        walk(j.get("testSteps"), 0)
        us = j.get("userStory", {})
        rows.append(dict(path=us.get("path", ""), story=us.get("storyName", ""), title=j.get("title") or j.get("name", ""),
                         result=j.get("result", ""), steps=steps, description=j.get("description") or ""))
    return rows


def flags(rows):
    out = []
    if not rows:
        return ["no outcome files found: run the tests first"]
    paths = {r["path"] for r in rows}
    stories = {r["story"] for r in rows}
    if len(rows) >= 4 and len(stories) == 1:
        out.append("all %d scenarios are in one group (%s): split them by feature" % (len(rows), next(iter(stories))))
    depths = {len(re.split(r"[/.]", p)) for p in paths if p}
    if len(rows) >= 6 and max(depths or {0}) < 2:
        out.append("no functional hierarchy: use packages/folders or @Epic/@Feature/@Story to group the scenarios")
    seen = {}
    for r in rows:
        seen.setdefault(r["title"].lower(), []).append(r["path"])
    for t, ps in seen.items():
        if len(ps) > 1:
            out.append("duplicate scenario title '%s' (%d times)" % (t, len(ps)))
    for st in sorted(stories):
        if re.search(r"[a-z]Test$|Tests$|^Test[A-Z]", st or ""):
            out.append("feature '%s' shows with its class name (\"%s\"): put @DisplayName with a business phrase on the class" % (st, re.sub(r"(?<!^)(?=[A-Z])", " ", st).lower()))
    for r in rows:
        t = r["title"]
        where = "%s: " % t
        if re.search(r"\d$", t) or re.match(r"test\b", t, re.I) or t.endswith("()") or "_" in t or " " not in t.strip():
            out.append(where + "title looks like a method name")
        if len(t.split()) < 3:
            out.append(where + "title is too short to state a rule or outcome")
        if SELECTOR.search(t) or HTTP.search(t) or URL.search(t):
            out.append(where + "title contains technical detail (selector, URL or status code)")
        if not r["steps"]:
            out.append(where + "no steps recorded (nothing for a reader to follow)")
        for _, d in r["steps"]:
            if SELECTOR.search(d):
                out.append(where + "step shows a selector or element id: '%s'" % d[:80])
            elif URL.search(d):
                out.append(where + "step shows a URL: '%s'" % d[:80])
            elif PLUMBING.search(d):
                out.append(where + "step is plumbing, not business language: '%s'" % d[:80])
            elif HTTP.search(d) and not re.search(r"\border\b|\bORD-", d, re.I):
                out.append(where + "step mentions an HTTP status: '%s'" % d[:80])
            elif re.match(r"^(click|type|enter|select|open|navigate)\w* ", d, re.I) and not re.search(r"\{|\b(she|he|they|\w+ (?:clicks|types|enters|opens))\b", d, re.I):
                out.append(where + "step is a bare UI action without an actor: '%s'" % d[:80])
    return sorted(set(out))


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    rows = load(sys.argv[1])
    fl = flags(rows)
    if "--json" in sys.argv:
        print(json.dumps(dict(scenarios=rows, flags=fl), indent=1))
        return
    tree = {}
    for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (r["path"], r["title"])):
        tree.setdefault(r["path"], []).append(r)
    for path, rs in tree.items():
        print(path.replace("/", " > ") or "(no group)")
        for r in rs:
            print("  - %s  [%s]" % (r["title"], r["result"]))
            for depth, d in r["steps"]:
                print("      %s%s" % ("  " * depth, d))
    print("\nFLAGS (%d)" % len(fl))
    for f in fl:
        print("  ! " + f)
    sys.exit(1 if fl else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### `living-docs/shop/browsing/WhenSearchingTheCatalogTest.java`

```java
package shop.browsing;

import net.serenitybdd.annotations.Step;
import net.serenitybdd.annotations.Steps;
import net.serenitybdd.junit5.SerenityJUnit5Extension;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.DisplayName;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)
@DisplayName("Searching the catalog")
class WhenSearchingTheCatalogTest {

    @Steps
    ShopperSteps shopper;

    @Test
    void searchingByTitleFindsTheMatchingBook() {
        shopper.searchesFor("Refactoring");
        shopper.shouldSeeBooks(1);
    }

    public static class ShopperSteps {
        private int found;

        @Step("Search the catalog for '{0}'")
        public void searchesFor(String term) { found = "Refactoring".equals(term) ? 1 : 0; }

        @Step("The catalog lists {0} book(s)")
        public void shouldSeeBooks(int expected) { assertThat(found).isEqualTo(expected); }
    }
}
```

### `living-docs/shop/ordering/AddToBasket.java`

```java
package shop.ordering;

import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.Actor;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.Performable;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.Task;

public class AddToBasket {
    public static Performable theBook(String title) {
        return Task.where("{0} adds '" + title + "' to the basket",
                actor -> actor.<Basket>recall("basket").add(title));
    }
}
```

### `living-docs/shop/ordering/Basket.java`

```java
package shop.ordering;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/** A tiny in-memory basket so the example needs no browser or server. */
public class Basket {
    private final List<String> titles = new ArrayList<>();
    public void add(String title) { titles.add(title); }
    public int size() { return titles.size(); }
    public boolean isEmpty() { return titles.isEmpty(); }
}
```

### `living-docs/shop/ordering/WhenAReaderBuildsABasketTest.java`

```java
package shop.ordering;

import net.serenitybdd.annotations.Narrative;
import net.serenitybdd.junit5.SerenityJUnit5Extension;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.Actor;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actors.OnStage;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actors.OnlineCast;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.DisplayName;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;

import static net.serenitybdd.screenplay.GivenWhenThen.seeThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)
@DisplayName("Building a basket")
@Narrative(text = {"As a reader", "I want to collect books in a basket", "So that I can buy them together"})
class WhenAReaderBuildsABasketTest {

    @BeforeEach
    void setTheStage() {
        OnStage.setTheStage(new OnlineCast());
    }

    @Test
    @DisplayName("A reader can add a book to an empty basket")
    void aReaderCanAddABookToAnEmptyBasket() {
        Actor ada = OnStage.theActorCalled("Ada");
        ada.remember("basket", new Basket());

        ada.attemptsTo(AddToBasket.theBook("The Pragmatic Programmer"));

        assertThat(ada.<Basket>recall("basket").size()).isEqualTo(1);
    }

    @Test
    void shouldKeepEveryBookAddedToTheBasket() {
        Actor ada = OnStage.theActorCalled("Ada");
        ada.remember("basket", new Basket());

        ada.attemptsTo(AddToBasket.theBook("Refactoring"), AddToBasket.theBook("Fluent Python"));

        assertThat(ada.<Basket>recall("basket").size()).isEqualTo(2);
    }
}
```

# Screenplay: Imports and Idioms

Verified against Serenity **5.4.1** (Playwright modules: **5.3.11**, the latest published). The examples at the end of this page compile and their tests pass.

Screenplay works with Selenium, Playwright and REST, with JUnit 5 or Cucumber. All of these are valid. Pick the one the user asked for or the project already uses, and don't mix them in one project.

## 1. Where things live

The packages are not guessable. Guessing them is the most common cause of compile errors.

### Core (all Screenplay projects), artifact `serenity-screenplay`
| Class | Package |
|---|---|
| `Actor`, `Task`, `Performable`, `Question`, `Interaction`, `Ability`, `Consequence`, `Tasks`, `RememberThat` | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay` |
| `GivenWhenThen` (`seeThat`) | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay` (use as a static import) |
| `OnStage`, `OnlineCast`, `Cast`, `Stage` | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actors` |
| `CastMember` | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.annotations` |
| `Check` (conditional tasks) | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.conditions` |
| `Wait`, `WaitUntil` | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.waits` |

### Selenium, artifact `serenity-screenplay-webdriver`
| Class | Package |
|---|---|
| `BrowseTheWeb` | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.abilities` |
| `Open`, `Click`, `Enter`, `Hit`, `Clear`, `Hover`, `Scroll`, `SelectFromOptions` | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actions` |
| `Target` | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.targets`. `Target.the("name").locatedBy("..")` takes a **String**. Serenity treats the string as XPath if it compiles as an XPath expression, otherwise as CSS. So `.new-todo`, `#id`, `[data-test=x]` and `li label` are CSS, but a tag-prefixed selector such as `input.new-todo`, `button` or `h1` is read as XPath and finds nothing. For those use `Target.the("name").located(By.cssSelector("input.new-todo"))` (or a leading `.`/`#`, or an explicit `//input[...]`). |
| `Text`, `TextContent`, `Value`, `Attribute`, `Visibility`, `Presence`, `Enabled`, `Disabled`, `SelectedValue`, `CurrentVisibility`, `WebElementQuestion` | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.questions` |

`Ensure` for web is in artifact `serenity-ensure`: **`net.serenitybdd.screenplay.ensure.Ensure`**.

### Playwright, artifact `serenity-screenplay-playwright`
Everything lives under `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright`:

| Class | Package |
|---|---|
| `BrowseTheWebWithPlaywright` | `...playwright.abilities` |
| `PlaywrightCast` (use instead of `OnlineCast`) | `...playwright.actors` |
| `Open`, `Click`, `Enter`, `Press`, `Navigate`, `Check`, `Hover`, `WaitFor` ... | `...playwright.interactions` |
| `Text`, `Visibility`, `Count`, `Attribute` ... | `...playwright.questions` |
| `Ensure` | `...playwright.assertions` |
| `Target` | `...playwright.Target` |

Playwright locators are plain Playwright selector strings (`".new-todo"`, `"text='Delete'"`) or a Playwright `Target`.

Playwright classes that exist (all take a selector string or a `Target`):

| Kind | Classes and entry points |
|---|---|
| Interactions (`...playwright.interactions`) | `Open.url(..)`, `Navigate`, `Click.on(..)`, `DoubleClick`, `RightClick`, `Hover.over(..)`, `Enter.theValue(..).into(..)`, `Press.keys("Enter")`, `Clear`, `Focus`, `Check.the(..)`, `Uncheck.checkbox(..)`, `SelectFromOptions.byVisibleText(..)` / `.byValue(..)` / `.byIndex(..)` then `.from(selector)`, `Upload`, `Drag`, `ScrollIntoView`, `WaitFor.selector(..)` |
| Questions (`...playwright.questions`) | `Text.of(..)`, `Text.ofEach(..)` (`List<String>`), `Value.of(..)`, `SelectedOptionText.of(..)`, `Checked.of(..)`, `Visibility.of(..)`, `Presence`, `Absence`, `Count.of(..)`, `Attribute`, `Enabled`, `Disabled`, `AllOptionTexts` |
| Assertions (`...playwright.assertions.Ensure`) | `Ensure.that(selector).isVisible() / isHidden() / hasText(..) / containsText(..) / hasValue(..) / isChecked() / hasCount(n) / hasAttribute(n, v)` |

**Don't use `Ensure.thatTheCurrentUrl()` or `Ensure.thatThePageTitle()`: they return package-private classes, and any call on them fails to compile** ("UrlEnsure.contains(java.lang.String) is defined in an inaccessible class or interface"; run in the verification script in the serenity-core repository (`docs/ai/skill`)). To check the URL, assert on the page: `assertThat(BrowseTheWebWithPlaywright.as(actor).getCurrentPage().url()).contains("/catalog")` (after `attemptsTo(..)`, in the test body), or better, check something the user sees on the new page (`Ensure.that("h1").hasText("Catalog")`).

**A selector must match exactly one element** for `WaitFor.selector`, `Click.on`, `Enter`, `Ensure.that(..).hasText(..)` and `Text.of(..)` (Playwright's strict mode). A selector that matches a list (`"#books .book"` with five rows) fails at run time with `strict mode violation: ... resolved to 5 elements`. For a list: wait on the first row (`"#books .book >> nth=0"`), count with `Ensure.that("#books .book").hasCount(5)`, read all texts with `Text.ofEach(..)`, pick one with `">> nth=0"` or `">> nth=-1"` (last), or narrow with `has-text`/`text-is` (`"tr.book:has(td.title:text-is('Refactoring'))"`). `sp-playwright/todo/ListTest.java` runs these.

**Don't build a Playwright text pattern with `Pattern.quote(..)`.** Playwright sends the pattern to the browser's JavaScript engine, which doesn't understand Java's `\Q..\E`, so `setHasText(Pattern.compile("^\\s*" + Pattern.quote(title) + "\\s*$"))` matches nothing and the step times out after 30 seconds (two Opus runs). Use the plain string (`setHasText(title)` matches by substring, ignoring case; `text-is('..')` / `has-text('..')` in a selector string match exactly or by substring), or write the pattern by hand (`Pattern.compile("^\\s*Clean Code\\s*$")`). Run in the verification script in the serenity-core repository (`docs/ai/skill`).

In a Playwright selector string a role needs the prefix: `"role=heading[name=\"Sign in\"]"`; without `role=` it throws `InvalidSelectorError` (run in the verification script in the serenity-core repository (`docs/ai/skill`)).

Playwright has no `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.ensure.Ensure` and no `Target` from `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.targets`: use the Playwright ones. See `sp-playwright/todo/FormTest.java`.

### REST, artifact `serenity-screenplay-rest`
| Class | Package |
|---|---|
| `CallAnApi` | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.rest.abilities` |
| `Get`, `Post`, `Delete`, `Ensure` ... | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.rest.interactions` |
| `LastResponse`, `TheResponse` | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.rest.questions` |

### Shared across all styles
| Class | Package |
|---|---|
| `@Managed`, `@Step`, `@Steps`, `@DefaultUrl`, `@WithTag` ... | `net.serenitybdd.annotations` (never `net.thucydides.core.annotations`) |
| `SerenityJUnit5Extension` | `net.serenitybdd.junit5` |
| `ScenarioSteps` (Page Objects) | `net.thucydides.core.steps` (**this one is correct** under `net.thucydides`) |

## 2. Common mistakes

| Wrong | Right |
|---|---|
| `import net.serenitybdd.rest.abilities.*` or `net.serenitybdd.rest.questions.*` for Screenplay REST (those packages don't exist) | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.rest.abilities.CallAnApi`, `...rest.questions.LastResponse` |
| `Target.the("x").locatedBy(By.id("x"))` | `locatedBy("#x")`, a String; for a `By` use `located(By.id("x"))` |
| `locatedBy("input.new-todo")` (tag-prefixed CSS; read as XPath, element not found at run time) | `located(By.cssSelector("input.new-todo"))` or `locatedBy(".new-todo")` | run-time failure, 5 of 66 unguided agentic runs |
| Two `public` classes in one file, or a class name different from its file name | One public class per file, and the file name equals the class name |
| `import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.webdriver.BrowseTheWeb` (package doesn't exist) | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.abilities.BrowseTheWeb` |
| `Question<List<String>>` returned from `Text.ofEach(target)` (Selenium) | `Question<Collection<String>>`. Playwright's `Text.ofEach` returns `List<String>` |
| `.viewedBy(actor)` on `Text`/`Value`/`Visibility`... | `actor.asksFor(Text.of(target))` or `Text.of(target).answeredBy(actor)`. `.viewedBy` is the old API |
| `net.thucydides.core.annotations.DefaultUrl` (and `Step`, `Managed`) | `net.serenitybdd.annotations.*` |
| JUnit 4 `@RunWith(SerenityRunner.class)` in a JUnit 5 project | `@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)` |
| Moving `ScenarioSteps` to `net.serenitybdd...` | `net.thucydides.core.steps.ScenarioSteps` |
| `OnlineCast` in the wrong package | `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actors.OnlineCast` |
| `@Page` annotation | Doesn't exist. In Page Object tests use `@Steps` for step libraries and extend `PageObject` for pages |
| `Instrumented` as a class | `Tasks.instrumented(MyTask.class, args)` (static method), or prefer `Task.where(..)` |
| `Ensure.thatTheCurrentUrl().contains(..)` or `Ensure.thatThePageTitle()` (Playwright) | Doesn't compile (package-private return types). Assert on `BrowseTheWebWithPlaywright.as(actor).getCurrentPage().url()` or on visible page content | 6 of the 8 guided Playwright compile failures inspected |
| `WaitFor.selector("#books .book")` or `Ensure.that("#books .book").hasText(..)` where the selector matches several rows | `"#books .book >> nth=0"`, or `hasCount(n)`, or `Text.ofEach(..)` | strict mode violation at run time, 2 guided runs |
| `Navigate` from a Selenium package | Selenium: `Open.url(..)`. `Navigate` exists only in Playwright |

## 3. Minimal working patterns

The source files are under `` and are compile-checked. Names are the same across styles so you can compare them.

| Style | Files | Key points |
|---|---|---|
| Screenplay + Selenium + JUnit 5 | `sp-selenium/todo/*` | `@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)`, `@Managed(driver="chrome") WebDriver`, `OnStage.setTheStage(new OnlineCast())`, `OnStage.theActorCalled("Toby")`, `Task.where(..)`, `Target.the(..).locatedBy(..)`, `seeThat(question, matcher)` or `Ensure.that(..)` |
| Screenplay + Playwright + JUnit 5 | `sp-playwright/todo/*` (todo list, form with select and checkbox) | `new PlaywrightCast()`, string selectors, `Press.keys("Enter")`, `Ensure.that(selector).hasText(..)` |
| Screenplay + REST + JUnit 5 | `sp-rest/api/*` | `Actor.named(..).whoCan(CallAnApi.at(baseUrl))`, `Get.resource(..)`, `Post.to(..).with(request -> ...)`, `LastResponse.received()` |
| Cucumber + Screenplay | `cuke-sp/*` | `@Suite` + `@IncludeEngines("cucumber")` + `@SelectClasspathResource("features")`, plugin `net.serenitybdd.cucumber.core.plugin.SerenityReporterParallel`, a `{actor}` `@ParameterType`, `@Before` that sets the stage |

### Rules of thumb
- Use `Task.where("{0} does something", step1, step2)` for tasks. Use a class with `performAs` only when the task needs real logic.
- `actor.attemptsTo(..)` for actions. `actor.should(seeThat(..))` or `Ensure` for checks.
- Keep locators in a `Target` holder class (Selenium) or constants (Playwright).
- Build tasks and questions with a static factory (`AddATodo.called("Buy milk")`) so the test reads like a sentence.

## 4. Not yet verified
- `Ensure` for web has several overloads. Only `that(Target).hasText(..)` is compile-tested.
- Page Objects (Selenium and Playwright) are covered in `page-objects.md`, not here.
- The examples were run once against the live sample sites with Serenity 5.4.1 (Playwright modules 5.3.11). Other sites and larger suites may behave differently.
- `serenity-screenplay-playwright` is documented at 5.3.11, not 5.4.x.

## Examples

These files compile against Serenity 5.4.1 (Playwright examples: 5.3.11).

### `sp-selenium/todo/AddATodo.java`

```java
package todo;

import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.Performable;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.Task;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actions.Enter;
import org.openqa.selenium.Keys;

public class AddATodo {
    public static Performable called(String item) {
        return Task.where("{0} adds a todo called " + item,
                Enter.theValue(item).into(TodoList.NEW_TODO).thenHit(Keys.ENTER));
    }
}
```

### `sp-selenium/todo/AddTodoTest.java`

```java
package todo;

import net.serenitybdd.annotations.Managed;
import net.serenitybdd.junit5.SerenityJUnit5Extension;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actions.Open;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actors.OnStage;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actors.OnlineCast;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.ensure.Ensure;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.openqa.selenium.WebDriver;

import static net.serenitybdd.screenplay.GivenWhenThen.seeThat;
import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.hasItem;

@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)
class AddTodoTest {

    @Managed(driver = "chrome")
    WebDriver browser;

    @BeforeEach
    void setTheStage() {
        OnStage.setTheStage(new OnlineCast());
    }

    @Test
    void shouldShowTheNewTodo() {
        var toby = OnStage.theActorCalled("Toby");
        toby.attemptsTo(
                Open.url("https://todo-app.serenity-js.org"),
                AddATodo.called("Buy milk"));
        toby.should(seeThat(TheTodos.displayed(), hasItem("Buy milk")));
    }

    @Test
    void shouldShowTheNewTodoUsingEnsure() {
        var toby = OnStage.theActorCalled("Toby");
        toby.attemptsTo(
                Open.url("https://todo-app.serenity-js.org"),
                AddATodo.called("Buy milk"),
                Ensure.that(TodoList.ITEMS).hasText("Buy milk"));
    }
}
```

### `sp-selenium/todo/TheTodos.java`

```java
package todo;

import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.Question;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.questions.Text;

import java.util.Collection;

public class TheTodos {
    // Text.ofEach(..) is a Question<Collection<String>> - not List<String>
    public static Question<Collection<String>> displayed() {
        return Text.ofEach(TodoList.ITEMS);
    }
}
```

### `sp-selenium/todo/TodoList.java`

```java
package todo;

import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.targets.Target;
import org.openqa.selenium.By;

public class TodoList {
    // locatedBy(String) treats a string as XPath whenever it compiles as one, so a CSS selector such as
    // "input.new-todo" (a valid XPath name) is NOT found. Use located(By.cssSelector(..)) for those.
    public static final Target NEW_TODO = Target.the("new todo field").located(By.cssSelector("input.new-todo"));
    public static final Target ITEMS = Target.the("todo items").locatedBy(".todo-list li label");
}
```

### `sp-playwright/todo/AddTodoTest.java`

```java
package todo;

import net.serenitybdd.junit5.SerenityJUnit5Extension;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.Performable;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.Task;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actors.OnStage;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.actors.PlaywrightCast;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.assertions.Ensure;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.interactions.Enter;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.interactions.Open;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.interactions.Press;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.questions.Text;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;

import static net.serenitybdd.screenplay.GivenWhenThen.seeThat;
import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.hasItem;

@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)
class AddTodoTest {

    static final String NEW_TODO = ".new-todo";
    static final String ITEMS = ".todo-list li label";

    static Performable addATodo(String item) {
        return Task.where("{0} adds a todo called " + item,
                Enter.theValue(item).into(NEW_TODO),
                Press.keys("Enter"));
    }

    @BeforeEach
    void setTheStage() {
        OnStage.setTheStage(new PlaywrightCast());
    }

    @Test
    void shouldShowTheNewTodo() {
        var toby = OnStage.theActorCalled("Toby");
        toby.attemptsTo(
                Open.url("https://todo-app.serenity-js.org"),
                addATodo("Buy milk"),
                Ensure.that(ITEMS).hasText("Buy milk"));
        // Playwright's Text.ofEach(..) is a Question<List<String>> (Selenium's is Collection<String>)
        toby.should(seeThat(Text.ofEach(ITEMS), hasItem("Buy milk")));
    }
}
```

### `sp-playwright/todo/FormTest.java`

```java
package todo;

import net.serenitybdd.junit5.SerenityJUnit5Extension;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actors.OnStage;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.actors.PlaywrightCast;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.assertions.Ensure;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.interactions.Check;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.interactions.Click;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.interactions.Open;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.interactions.SelectFromOptions;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.interactions.WaitFor;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.questions.Checked;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.questions.SelectedOptionText;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.questions.Value;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;

import static net.serenitybdd.screenplay.GivenWhenThen.seeThat;
import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.equalTo;

/** Playwright interactions and questions for forms. Selectors are Playwright selector strings. */
@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)
class FormTest {

    // A self-contained page, so the example runs without a network or a site
    static final String FORM_PAGE = "data:text/html,"
            + "<select id='country'><option value='us'>United States</option><option value='ca'>Canada</option></select>"
            + "<input type='checkbox' id='terms'><button id='submit'>Send</button>";

    @BeforeEach
    void setTheStage() {
        OnStage.setTheStage(new PlaywrightCast());
    }

    @Test
    void shouldFillInAForm() {
        var ana = OnStage.theActorCalled("Ana");
        ana.attemptsTo(
                Open.url(FORM_PAGE),
                SelectFromOptions.byVisibleText("Canada").from("#country"),   // also byValue(..), byIndex(..)
                Check.the("#terms"),                                          // Uncheck.checkbox(..) to clear
                WaitFor.selector("#submit"),
                Click.on("#submit"),
                Ensure.that("#country").hasValue("ca"),
                Ensure.that("#terms").isChecked());
        ana.should(
                seeThat(SelectedOptionText.of("#country"), equalTo("Canada")),
                seeThat(Value.of("#country"), equalTo("ca")),
                seeThat(Checked.of("#terms")));
    }
}
```

### `sp-playwright/todo/ListTest.java`

```java
package todo;

import net.serenitybdd.junit5.SerenityJUnit5Extension;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actors.OnStage;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.actors.PlaywrightCast;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.assertions.Ensure;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.interactions.Open;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.interactions.WaitFor;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright.questions.Text;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.DisplayName;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;

import java.util.List;

import static net.serenitybdd.screenplay.GivenWhenThen.seeThat;
import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.contains;

/**
 * A selector used by WaitFor, Click, Ensure.hasText and Text.of must match exactly ONE element (Playwright's strict mode).
 * For a list, wait on the first row, count with hasCount, read all texts with Text.ofEach, or pick one with ">> nth=N".
 */
@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)
@DisplayName("Reading a list on a page")
class ListTest {

    static final String LIST_PAGE = "data:text/html,<table><tbody id='rows'>"
            + "<tr class='row'><td class='title'>Fluent Python</td></tr>"
            + "<tr class='row'><td class='title'>Clean Code</td></tr>"
            + "<tr class='row'><td class='title'>Refactoring</td></tr></tbody></table>";

    @BeforeEach
    void setTheStage() {
        OnStage.setTheStage(new PlaywrightCast());
    }

    @Test
    @DisplayName("The rows of a list can be counted, read and picked by position")
    void rowsCanBeCountedReadAndPickedByPosition() {
        var ana = OnStage.theActorCalled("Ana");
        ana.attemptsTo(
                Open.url(LIST_PAGE),
                WaitFor.selector("#rows .row >> nth=0"),            // not "#rows .row": that matches 3 elements and fails
                Ensure.that("#rows .row").hasCount(3),              // hasCount is the check for "how many"
                Ensure.that("#rows .row >> nth=0 >> .title").hasText("Fluent Python"),
                Ensure.that("#rows .row >> nth=-1 >> .title").hasText("Refactoring"));
        ana.should(seeThat(Text.ofEach("#rows .title"), contains("Fluent Python", "Clean Code", "Refactoring")));
    }
}
```

### `sp-rest/api/UsersApi.java`

```java
package api;

import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.Performable;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.Task;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.rest.interactions.Get;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.rest.interactions.Post;

public class UsersApi {
    public static Performable fetchUser(int id) {
        return Task.where("{0} fetches user " + id, Get.resource("/users/" + id));
    }

    public static Performable createPost(String title) {
        return Task.where("{0} creates a post titled " + title,
                Post.to("/posts").with(request -> request
                        .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
                        .body("{\"title\":\"" + title + "\",\"body\":\"text\",\"userId\":1}")));
    }
}
```

### `sp-rest/api/UsersApiTest.java`

```java
package api;

import net.serenitybdd.junit5.SerenityJUnit5Extension;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.Actor;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.rest.abilities.CallAnApi;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.rest.questions.LastResponse;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;

import static net.serenitybdd.screenplay.GivenWhenThen.seeThat;
import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.equalTo;

@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)
class UsersApiTest {

    Actor alice;

    @BeforeEach
    void setUp() {
        alice = Actor.named("Alice").whoCan(CallAnApi.at("https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com"));
    }

    @Test
    void shouldFindUserOne() {
        alice.attemptsTo(UsersApi.fetchUser(1));
        alice.should(
                seeThat("the status code", actor -> LastResponse.received().answeredBy(actor).statusCode(), equalTo(200)),
                seeThat("the user name", actor -> LastResponse.received().answeredBy(actor).path("name"), equalTo("Leanne Graham")));
    }

    @Test
    void shouldCreateAPost() {
        alice.attemptsTo(UsersApi.createPost("Hello"));
        alice.should(seeThat("the status code", actor -> LastResponse.received().answeredBy(actor).statusCode(), equalTo(201)));
    }
}
```

### `cuke-sp/todo/TodoStepDefinitions.java`

```java
package todo;

import io.cucumber.java.Before;
import io.cucumber.java.ParameterType;
import io.cucumber.java.en.Given;
import io.cucumber.java.en.Then;
import io.cucumber.java.en.When;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.Actor;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actions.Open;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actors.OnStage;
import net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actors.OnlineCast;

import static net.serenitybdd.screenplay.GivenWhenThen.seeThat;
import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.hasItem;

public class TodoStepDefinitions {

    @Before
    public void setTheStage() {
        OnStage.setTheStage(new OnlineCast());
    }

    @ParameterType(".*")
    public Actor actor(String name) {
        return OnStage.theActorCalled(name);
    }

    @Given("{actor} has opened the todo app")
    public void opensTheApp(Actor actor) {
        actor.attemptsTo(Open.url("https://todo-app.serenity-js.org"));
    }

    @When("{actor} adds {string} to the list")
    public void addsATodo(Actor actor, String item) {
        actor.attemptsTo(AddATodo.called(item));
    }

    @Then("{actor} should see {string} in the list")
    public void seesTheTodo(Actor actor, String item) {
        actor.should(seeThat(TheTodos.displayed(), hasItem(item)));
    }
}
```

# Cucumber: Runner, Tags, Hooks, Gradle and Parallel

Verified against Serenity **5.4.1** (Cucumber 8.0.4, JUnit 6.1.3). Every command on this page was run against the example at the end of the page.

## 1. Setup

- **Maven:** the Cucumber row of the dependency table on the project-setup page: `serenity-core`, `serenity-junit5`, `serenity-cucumber`, `io.cucumber:cucumber-java`, `io.cucumber:cucumber-junit-platform-engine`, `junit-platform-suite`. Use the JUnit BOM, and use the Cucumber version Serenity brings.
- **Gradle:** the `build.gradle` at the end of this page is a working build (below).
- Feature files go in `src/test/resources/features`, step definitions and hooks in a package under `src/test/java`.

## 2. The runner

A JUnit Platform suite. No `@RunWith`:

```java
@Suite
@IncludeEngines("cucumber")
@SelectClasspathResource("features")
@ConfigurationParameter(key = GLUE_PROPERTY_NAME, value = "demo")   // the package(s) with steps and hooks
@ConfigurationParameter(key = PLUGIN_PROPERTY_NAME, value = "net.serenitybdd.cucumber.core.plugin.SerenityReporterParallel,pretty")
public class RunCucumberTests {
}
```

- The plugin class is `net.serenitybdd.cucumber.core.plugin.SerenityReporterParallel`. It connects Cucumber to Serenity: without it, Serenity APIs used in steps fail with "No BaseStepListener has been registered".
- Name the class so that Maven's test plugin runs it: ending in `Test` or `Tests` (`RunCucumberTests`). A name such as `CucumberSuite` is skipped silently (see the troubleshooting page, "Results: 0 tests").
- `@RunWith(CucumberWithSerenity.class)` (from `net.serenitybdd.cucumber`) is the JUnit 4 style runner. In a JUnit 5 project use the suite above.

## 3. Running part of the suite

All of these were run against the example. Add them to the Maven command line:

| Goal | Option | Scenarios run (of 5) |
|---|---|---|
| Only `@smoke` | `-Dcucumber.filter.tags=@smoke` |
| Everything except `@wip` | `-Dcucumber.filter.tags="not @wip"` |
| Tag expression | `-Dcucumber.filter.tags="@basket and not @wip"` |
| By scenario name (regular expression) | `-Dcucumber.filter.name="Adding passes"` |
| One feature file | `-Dcucumber.features=src/test/resources/features/basket.feature` |

The same filters can be fixed in the project instead of the command line:

- in the runner: `@ConfigurationParameter(key = FILTER_TAGS_PROPERTY_NAME, value = "not @wip")` (`Constants.FILTER_TAGS_PROPERTY_NAME`, the same class as `GLUE_PROPERTY_NAME`): 4 scenarios, or
- in `src/test/resources/junit-platform.properties`: `cucumber.filter.tags=not @wip`: 4 scenarios.

When `cucumber.features` is given, Cucumber ignores the runner's `@SelectClasspathResource` and prints a warning saying so; that is expected.

**Re-running failed scenarios.** Add the Cucumber `rerun` plugin to the runner (`...SerenityReporterParallel,pretty,rerun:target/rerun.txt`). After a run that has failures, `target/rerun.txt` lists them (`classpath:features/failing.feature:3`). Run only those with `-Dcucumber.features=@target/rerun.txt` (verified: 6 scenarios, then 1).

## 4. Gradle

the `build.gradle` at the end of this page (Serenity Gradle plugin `net.serenity-bdd.serenity-gradle-plugin` 5.4.1, Gradle 9.8.1 tested, tasks `test` and `aggregate`) was run: `gradle clean test` ran the 5 scenarios and `aggregate` produced `target/site/serenity/index.html`.

**Gradle does not pass `-D` options to the test JVM.** `gradle test -Dcucumber.filter.tags=@smoke` runs every scenario unless the build forwards the option (verified: 4 outcomes without it, 1 with it):

```groovy
test {
    useJUnitPlatform()
    systemProperties System.properties.findAll { k, v -> k.toString().startsWith('cucumber.') }
    finalizedBy 'aggregate'
}
```

The same applies to any other `-D` option your tests read. `ignoreFailures = true` in that file lets the report task run when a scenario fails (the same idea as `-Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=true` for Maven); leave it out if the build must fail.

## 5. Scenario outlines, data tables and parameter types

`cuke-plain/features/maths.feature` has a `Scenario Outline` with an `Examples` table (2 rows) and `basket.feature` has a `Background` and a data table. In the steps (`BasketSteps.java`):

- a data table argument is `io.cucumber.datatable.DataTable` (`items.asMaps()` gives a list of rows);
- a custom parameter type is a method annotated `@ParameterType("\\d+\\.\\d+")` that returns the type (`{money}` in the step text gives a `BigDecimal`);
- Maven counts each example row as a scenario (the example has 5: 1 + 2 + 2); the Serenity outcome files (`target/site/serenity/*.json`) count the outline once (4 files for these 5 scenarios), so two counts of the same run can differ.

## 6. Hooks

`cuke-plain/demo/Hooks.java`:

- `@Before` and `@After` from `io.cucumber.java`; they take an optional `io.cucumber.java.Scenario` argument (`getName()`, `getSourceTagNames()`, `isFailed()`, `getStatus()`).
- `@Before("@basket")` runs only for scenarios with that tag; `order` sorts hooks: `@Before` hooks run from the lowest order to the highest, `@After` hooks from the highest to the lowest (verified: before-1, before-5, after-5, after-1).
- `Serenity.recordReportData().withTitle("..").andContents("..")` adds data to the scenario in the Serenity report (checked: it appears in the outcome files).

## 7. Sharing state between steps

Cucumber creates new step-definition objects for every scenario. Three ways to share state inside one scenario:

1. **Fields of one step class.** Fine when all the steps are in that class.
2. **Serenity session variables** (used in the example): `Serenity.setSessionVariable("basketTotal").to(value)` and `Serenity.sessionVariableCalled("basketTotal")`. They are per scenario (and per thread) and work from any class.
3. **Dependency injection with PicoContainer:** add `io.cucumber:cucumber-picocontainer` (same version as Cucumber), give each step class a constructor that takes the shared object, and Cucumber creates one instance per scenario (verified with two step classes sharing a `Shared` object).

Do not use static fields to share scenario state: with parallel execution scenarios overwrite each other.

## 8. Parallel execution

`src/test/resources/junit-platform.properties`:

```
cucumber.execution.parallel.enabled=true
cucumber.execution.parallel.config.strategy=fixed
cucumber.execution.parallel.config.fixed.parallelism=4
```

Verified: the 5 scenarios ran and the report was produced. Keep in mind that each scenario needs its own state (section 7) and, in a web test, its own browser. Reports of parallel runs are a common source of problems; the troubleshooting page says what has and has not been reproduced.

## 9. Cucumber with Screenplay

Put `OnStage.setTheStage(new OnlineCast())` in a `@Before` hook and a `@ParameterType` named `actor` that returns `OnStage.theActorCalled(name)`, as in the Screenplay page's Cucumber example.

## 10. Cucumber with page objects and a step library (no Screenplay)

The glue code is thin: each step definition calls one `@Step` method of a step library, and the step library uses a page object. The example `cuke-pages` has the whole chain (`SignInStepDefinitions` -> `ReaderSteps` -> `SignInPage`) and its 3 scenarios pass in headless Chrome; the verification script in the serenity-core repository (`docs/ai/skill`) runs the claims below.

- Declare the library in the step-definition class with **`@Steps ReaderSteps reader;`** (`net.serenitybdd.annotations.Steps`). Declare the page object as a plain field of the step library (`SignInPage signInPage;`); Serenity creates it and gives it the driver. With `ReaderSteps reader = new ReaderSteps();` the page field stays null and the scenario errors with `NullPointerException: ... "this.signInPage" is null`.
- Page objects extend `net.serenitybdd.core.pages.PageObject` and use `@FindBy` with `WebElementFacade`; no `@Managed` is needed in Cucumber. See `page-objects.md` for the idioms.
- The report shows both layers: the Gherkin line ("When Reader signs in as ...") with the `@Step` text nested under it ("Sign in as reader@example.com with the password wrong"). Write the `@Step` text in business language too.
- The runner and plugin are the same as in section 2: the plugin class is `net.serenitybdd.cucumber.core.plugin.SerenityReporterParallel`.

### Optional text `book(s)` in a Cucumber expression

In a step written `@Then("the catalogue lists {int} book(s)")`, `(s)` is **optional text**: the step matches "5 book" and "5 books". It does **not** match a feature line that contains the characters `book(s)`. Reproduced: a feature saying `the catalogue lists 5 book(s)` gave `The step 'the catalogue lists 5 book(s)' is undefined.` and Maven failed the build, while the Serenity report shows the scenario as **pending** (not failed), so look at the console output as well as the report. Write the feature in plain words ("1 book", "5 books"); to match a literal `(s)`, escape it in the step as `book\\(s)`.

## 11. Not covered here

Gherkin in other languages, `@Before` for browser start-up in cloud grids, the Cucumber `Transpose`/`DocString` types, Spring or Guice object factories, and Cucumber-JVM versions other than the one Serenity brings.

These files compile against Serenity 5.4.1 (Playwright examples: 5.3.11).

### `cuke-plain/demo/BasketSteps.java`

```java
package demo;

import io.cucumber.datatable.DataTable;
import io.cucumber.java.ParameterType;
import io.cucumber.java.en.Given;
import io.cucumber.java.en.Then;
import io.cucumber.java.en.When;
import net.serenitybdd.core.Serenity;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

public class BasketSteps {

    // A custom parameter type: "3.70 dollars" -> BigDecimal
    @ParameterType("\\d+\\.\\d+")
    public BigDecimal money(String amount) {
        return new BigDecimal(amount);
    }

    @Given("an empty basket")
    public void anEmptyBasket() {
        // Serenity session variables live for one scenario and can be read from any step class
        Serenity.setSessionVariable("basketTotal").to(BigDecimal.ZERO);
    }

    @When("I add these items:")
    public void iAddTheseItems(DataTable items) {
        List<Map<String, String>> rows = items.asMaps();
        for (Map<String, String> row : rows) {
            addToTotal(new BigDecimal(row.get("price")));
        }
    }

    @When("I add a {string} costing {money} dollars")
    public void iAddACosting(String name, BigDecimal price) {
        addToTotal(price);
    }

    @Then("the basket total should be {money} dollars")
    public void theTotalShouldBe(BigDecimal expected) {
        BigDecimal total = Serenity.sessionVariableCalled("basketTotal");
        assertThat(total).isEqualByComparingTo(expected);
    }

    private void addToTotal(BigDecimal price) {
        BigDecimal total = Serenity.sessionVariableCalled("basketTotal");
        Serenity.setSessionVariable("basketTotal").to(total.add(price));
    }
}
```

### `cuke-plain/demo/Hooks.java`

```java
package demo;

import io.cucumber.java.After;
import io.cucumber.java.Before;
import io.cucumber.java.Scenario;
import net.serenitybdd.core.Serenity;

public class Hooks {

    // Runs before every scenario. The Scenario parameter is optional.
    @Before(order = 0)
    public void beforeEachScenario(Scenario scenario) {
        Serenity.recordReportData().withTitle("Scenario tags").andContents(String.join(", ", scenario.getSourceTagNames()));
    }

    // Only for scenarios tagged @basket
    @Before(value = "@basket", order = 1)
    public void beforeBasketScenarios() {
        Serenity.recordReportData().withTitle("Setup").andContents("basket scenario");
    }

    @After
    public void afterEachScenario(Scenario scenario) {
        if (scenario.isFailed()) {
            Serenity.recordReportData().withTitle("Failed scenario").andContents(scenario.getName());
        }
    }
}
```
