### `cuke-pages/shop/ReaderSteps.java`

```java
package shop;

import net.serenitybdd.annotations.Step;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

/** The step library: business-level steps that use the page object. Cucumber's glue code calls these. */
public class ReaderSteps {

    SignInPage signInPage;   // page objects are created for you when declared as fields

    @Step("Open the sign-in page")
    public void opensTheSignInPage() {
        signInPage.show();
    }

    @Step("Sign in as {0} with the password {1}")
    public void signsInWith(String email, String password) {
        signInPage.signInWith(email, password);
    }

    @Step("The {0} page should be shown")
    public void shouldSeeThePage(String name) {
        assertThat(signInPage.headingText()).isEqualTo(name);
    }

    @Step("The message {0} should be shown")
    public void shouldBeToldThat(String message) {
        assertThat(signInPage.messageText()).isEqualTo(message);
    }
}
```

### `cuke-pages/shop/SignInPage.java`

```java
package shop;

import net.serenitybdd.core.pages.PageObject;
import net.serenitybdd.core.pages.WebElementFacade;
import org.openqa.selenium.support.FindBy;

// A small page served from a data: URL, so the example needs no server or network.
public class SignInPage extends PageObject {
    static final String HTML = "<html><head><title>Bookshop</title></head><body>"
            + "<h1 id='heading'>Sign in</h1>"
            + "<input id='email'><input id='password' type='password'>"
            + "<button id='go' onclick=\"if (document.getElementById('password').value == 'correct-horse') {"
            + "document.getElementById('heading').innerText='Catalogue';"
            + "document.getElementById('error').innerText='5 books'} else {"
            + "document.getElementById('error').innerText='Invalid email or password'}\">Sign in</button>"
            + "<p id='error'></p></body></html>";

    @FindBy(id = "email")
    WebElementFacade email;

    @FindBy(id = "password")
    WebElementFacade password;

    @FindBy(id = "go")
    WebElementFacade signInButton;

    @FindBy(id = "heading")
    WebElementFacade heading;

    @FindBy(id = "error")
    WebElementFacade message;

    public void show() {
        getDriver().get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + HTML.replace("#", "%23"));
    }

    public void signInWith(String emailAddress, String secret) {
        email.type(emailAddress);
        password.type(secret);
        signInButton.click();
    }

    public String headingText() {
        return heading.getText();
    }

    public String messageText() {
        return message.getText();
    }
}
```

### `cuke-pages/shop/SignInStepDefinitions.java`

```java
package shop;

import io.cucumber.java.en.Given;
import io.cucumber.java.en.Then;
import io.cucumber.java.en.When;
import net.serenitybdd.annotations.Steps;

public class SignInStepDefinitions {

    @Steps
    ReaderSteps reader;

    @Given("Reader is on the sign-in page")
    public void readerIsOnTheSignInPage() {
        reader.opensTheSignInPage();
    }

    @When("Reader signs in as {string} with the password {string}")
    public void readerSignsIn(String email, String password) {
        reader.signsInWith(email, password);
    }

    @Then("the {word} page is shown")
    public void thePageIsShown(String name) {
        reader.shouldSeeThePage(name);
    }

    @Then("Reader is told {string}")
    public void readerIsTold(String message) {
        reader.shouldBeToldThat(message);
    }

    // "book(s)" is optional text in a Cucumber expression: this step matches "5 book" and "5 books",
    // but NOT the literal text "5 book(s)" if a feature file contains it.
    @Then("the catalogue lists {int} book(s)")
    public void theCatalogueLists(int count) {
        reader.shouldBeToldThat(count + " books");
    }
}
```

<!-- https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_page_object_idioms -->

# Page Objects: Imports and Idioms

Verified against Serenity **5.4.1** (Playwright module: **5.3.11**, the latest published). The examples at the end of this page compile and their tests pass.

Page Objects with step libraries work with Selenium and with Playwright, with JUnit 5. This is as valid as Screenplay. Use the style the user asked for or the project already uses, and don't mix Page Objects and Screenplay in one test.

## 1. Structure

```
Test (@Steps field)  ->  Step library (@Step methods)  ->  Page Object (locators and page actions)
```

Tests call step methods that read like business actions. Page Objects hide locators.

## 2. Where things live

| Class | Package |
|---|---|
| `@Step`, `@Steps`, `@Managed`, `@DefaultUrl`, `@WhenPageOpens`, `@WithTag`, `@Title`, `@Narrative`, `@Pending` | `net.serenitybdd.annotations` (**never** `net.thucydides.core.annotations`) |
| `SerenityJUnit5Extension` | `net.serenitybdd.junit5` |
| `PageObject`, `WebElementFacade` | `net.serenitybdd.core.pages` |
| `UIInteractionSteps` (base class for Selenium step libraries) | `net.serenitybdd.core.steps` |
| `Serenity` (static facade) | `net.serenitybdd.core.Serenity` |
| `ScenarioSteps` (older step library base class, still valid) | `net.thucydides.core.steps` |
| `Pages` | `net.thucydides.core.pages` |
| `@FindBy` | `org.openqa.selenium.support.FindBy` (Serenity also has `net.serenitybdd.core.annotations.findby.FindBy`) |

`net.thucydides.core.pages.WebElementFacade` and `net.thucydides.core.annotations.findby.FindBy` are deprecated aliases. Use the `net.serenitybdd` ones.

Maven: Selenium needs `serenity-core` and `serenity-junit5`. Playwright adds `serenity-playwright` and `com.microsoft.playwright:playwright`.

## 3. Selenium Page Objects

Files: `po-selenium/todo/{TodoPage,TodoSteps,AddTodoTest}.java`

- Page: `@DefaultUrl("https://...")`, `extends PageObject`, `@FindBy(css = "...") WebElementFacade field;`, or `$("css")`, `$$("css")` for lookups. **A String that starts with a tag name is not read as CSS.** `$("button")`, `$("th[data-sort='title']")` and `thenFind("button")` compile as XPath, so they look for the wrong thing and fail with `ElementShouldBeEnabledException` or `NoSuchElementException ... xpath`. Start the selector with `#` or `.` (`$("#go")`, `$(".sort")`), or use `$(By.cssSelector("button"))` (for a child element `row.findBy(By.cssSelector("button"))`; `thenFind` has no `By` version), or write a real XPath. The same rule applies to Screenplay `Target.the("name").locatedBy(..)`.
- **Don't write your own `open()`.** `PageObject.open()` already exists and opens the `@DefaultUrl`; it is `final`, so redeclaring it fails to compile. For another URL use `openAt("https://...")`, or a differently named method.
- `@FindBy(css = ...)` takes a String. `$(By.cssSelector(..))` takes a `By`. Don't mix them up.
- Step library: `extends UIInteractionSteps`, a field for each page object (injected automatically), and `@Step("Add the todo '{0}'")` on public methods. `{0}` is the first argument.
- Test: `@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)`, `@Managed(driver = "chrome") WebDriver driver;`, `@Steps TodoSteps todo;`. Assertions in the test with AssertJ or Hamcrest, or with `assertThat` inside a `@Step` method.
- Useful `WebElementFacade` methods: `type(..)`, `typeAndEnter(..)`, `click()`, `getText()`, `isVisible()`, `waitUntilVisible()`, `selectByVisibleText(..)`, `getValue()`.

## 4. Playwright Page Objects

Files: `po-playwright/todo/{TodoPage,TodoSteps,AddTodoTest}.java`

- The Page Object is a plain class that holds a `com.microsoft.playwright.Page`. It does **not** extend `PageObject`, and doesn't use `@FindBy`, `WebElementFacade` or `@DefaultUrl`. Locators are Playwright `page.locator("css")`, `getByRole(..)`.
- A locator used with `click()`, `fill()`, `textContent()` or `waitFor()` must match exactly one element (strict mode); for lists use `.first()`, `.nth(i)`, `.count()` or `allTextContents()`. **Don't build a Playwright text pattern with `Pattern.quote(..)`.** Playwright sends the pattern to the browser's JavaScript engine, which doesn't understand Java's `\Q..\E`, so `setHasText(Pattern.compile("^\\s*" + Pattern.quote(title) + "\\s*$"))` matches nothing and the step times out after 30 seconds (two Opus runs). Use the plain string (`setHasText(title)` matches by substring, ignoring case; `text-is('..')` / `has-text('..')` in a selector string match exactly or by substring), or write the pattern by hand (`Pattern.compile("^\\s*Clean Code\\s*$")`). Run in the verification script in the serenity-core repository (`docs/ai/skill`).
- Playwright Java API details models get wrong (run in the verification script in the serenity-core repository (`docs/ai/skill`)): `page.getByRole(role, new Page.GetByRoleOptions()...)` but `locator.getByRole(role, new Locator.GetByRoleOptions()...)`: passing the `Page` options to a locator is a compile error; and as a selector string a role needs the prefix, `"role=heading[name=\"Sign in\"]"`: `"heading[name=...]"` throws `InvalidSelectorError`.
- The test owns the browser: start `Playwright` and the `Browser` in `@BeforeAll`, and in `@BeforeEach` create a page and call `PlaywrightSerenity.registerPage(page)`. In `@AfterEach` call `PlaywrightSerenity.unregisterPage(page)` and close the page.
- Step library: a plain class with `@Step` methods that get the page from `PlaywrightSerenity.getCurrentPage()` (or take a `Page` parameter) and wrap it in the Page Object. No `UIInteractionSteps`.
- `PlaywrightSerenity` is in `net.serenitybdd.playwright`. A `@SerenityPlaywright` meta-annotation (`net.serenitybdd.playwright.junit5`) combines the extensions. See `serenity-playwright-demo` for it.

## 5. Common mistakes

| Wrong | Right |
|---|---|
| `import net.thucydides.core.annotations.{Step,Steps,Managed,DefaultUrl}` (most Page Object failures) | `net.serenitybdd.annotations.*` |
| Declaring `public void open()` in a page object | Delete it. Use the inherited `open()` with `@DefaultUrl`, or `openAt(url)` |
| `@FindBy("...")` or passing a String where a `By` is needed (and the reverse) | `@FindBy(css = "...")`; `$("css")` for Strings; `$(By.id("x"))` for a `By` |
| `$("button")`, `$("th[data-sort='title']")`, `row.thenFind("button")` (read as XPath) | `$("#go")`, `$(By.cssSelector("button"))`, `row.findBy(By.cssSelector("button"))` |
| JUnit 4 `@RunWith(SerenityRunner.class)` | `@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)` |
| `@Page` annotation | Doesn't exist. Use a page object field in the step library, or `@Steps` for step libraries in the test |
| `ScenarioSteps` from `net.serenitybdd...` | `net.thucydides.core.steps.ScenarioSteps` (this one *is* under `net.thucydides`) |
| Extending `PageObject` for a Playwright page, or `Page` from Selenium | Playwright pages are plain classes using `com.microsoft.playwright.Page` |

## 6. Not yet verified
- Runtime behaviour beyond the examples: they ran once against the live todo app.
- `@WhenPageOpens`, `waitFor`/`waitUntil*` helpers and `Pages`-based injection are not covered by examples.
- The Playwright section is based on 5.3.11 and the `serenity-playwright-demo` module.

## Examples

These files compile against Serenity 5.4.1 (Playwright examples: 5.3.11).

### `po-selenium/todo/AddTodoTest.java`

```java
package todo;

import net.serenitybdd.annotations.Managed;
import net.serenitybdd.annotations.Steps;
import net.serenitybdd.junit5.SerenityJUnit5Extension;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.openqa.selenium.WebDriver;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)
class AddTodoTest {

    @Managed(driver = "chrome")
    WebDriver driver;

    @Steps
    TodoSteps todo;

    @Test
    void shouldShowTheNewTodo() {
        todo.openTheApplication();
        todo.addTodo("Buy milk");
        assertThat(todo.todoItems()).contains("Buy milk");
    }
}
```

### `po-selenium/todo/TodoPage.java`

```java
package todo;

import net.serenitybdd.annotations.DefaultUrl;
import net.serenitybdd.core.pages.PageObject;
import net.serenitybdd.core.pages.WebElementFacade;
import org.openqa.selenium.support.FindBy;

import java.util.List;

// Do not declare your own open(): PageObject already has open() and it uses @DefaultUrl.
@DefaultUrl("https://todo-app.serenity-js.org")
public class TodoPage extends PageObject {

    @FindBy(css = ".new-todo")
    WebElementFacade newTodoField;

    public void addTodo(String item) {
        newTodoField.typeAndEnter(item);
    }

    public List<String> todoItems() {
        return $$(".todo-list li label").stream().map(WebElementFacade::getText).toList();
    }
}
```

### `po-selenium/todo/TodoSteps.java`

```java
package todo;

import net.serenitybdd.annotations.Step;
import net.serenitybdd.core.steps.UIInteractionSteps;

import java.util.List;

public class TodoSteps extends UIInteractionSteps {

    TodoPage todoPage;   // page objects are injected into step libraries

    @Step("Open the todo application")
    public void openTheApplication() {
        todoPage.open();
    }

    @Step("Add the todo '{0}'")
    public void addTodo(String item) {
        todoPage.addTodo(item);
    }

    public List<String> todoItems() {
        return todoPage.todoItems();
    }
}
```

### `po-playwright/todo/AddTodoTest.java`

```java
package todo;

import com.microsoft.playwright.Browser;
import com.microsoft.playwright.BrowserType;
import com.microsoft.playwright.Page;
import com.microsoft.playwright.Playwright;
import net.serenitybdd.annotations.Steps;
import net.serenitybdd.junit5.SerenityJUnit5Extension;
import net.serenitybdd.playwright.PlaywrightSerenity;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterAll;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeAll;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)
class AddTodoTest {

    @Steps
    TodoSteps todo;

    static Playwright playwright;
    static Browser browser;
    Page page;

    @BeforeAll
    static void startBrowser() {
        playwright = Playwright.create();
        browser = playwright.chromium().launch(new BrowserType.LaunchOptions().setHeadless(true));
    }

    @AfterAll
    static void stopBrowser() {
        browser.close();
        playwright.close();
    }

    @BeforeEach
    void openPage() {
        page = browser.newPage();
        PlaywrightSerenity.registerPage(page);   // lets Serenity report screenshots and steps
    }

    @AfterEach
    void closePage() {
        PlaywrightSerenity.unregisterPage(page);
        page.close();
    }

    @Test
    void shouldShowTheNewTodo() {
        todo.openTheApplication();
        todo.addTodo("Buy milk");
        assertThat(todo.todoItems()).contains("Buy milk");
    }
}
```

### `po-playwright/todo/TodoPage.java`

```java
package todo;

import com.microsoft.playwright.Page;

import java.util.List;

/** A plain class that wraps a Playwright Page. It does not extend Serenity's PageObject. */
public class TodoPage {

    private final Page page;

    public TodoPage(Page page) {
        this.page = page;
    }

    public void open() {
        page.navigate("https://todo-app.serenity-js.org");
    }

    public void addTodo(String item) {
        page.locator(".new-todo").fill(item);
        page.locator(".new-todo").press("Enter");
    }

    public List<String> todoItems() {
        return page.locator(".todo-list li label").allInnerTexts();
    }
}
```

### `po-playwright/todo/TodoSteps.java`

```java
package todo;

import com.microsoft.playwright.Page;

import net.serenitybdd.playwright.PlaywrightSerenity;

import java.util.List;

public class TodoSteps {

    }

    @Step("Open the todo application")
    public void openTheApplication() {
        todoPage().open();
    }

    @Step("Add the todo '{0}'")
    public void addTodo(String item) {
        todoPage().addTodo(item);
    }

    public List<String> todoItems() {
        return todoPage().todoItems();
    }
}
```

# REST with SerenityRest and a Step Library

Verified against Serenity **5.4.1**. The example at the end of this page compiles and its tests pass; each claim was run.

This is one of several valid ways to test a REST API with Serenity. The other is Screenplay with `CallAnApi` (see `screenplay.md` and `sp-rest/`). Use the one the user asked for or the project already uses; don't mix them.

## What you need

Artifact `serenity-rest-assured` (it brings REST-assured and Hamcrest), plus `serenity-core` and `serenity-junit5` as in `project-setup.md`. Do not pin REST-assured or Groovy versions (see `troubleshooting.md`).

## Where things live

| Class | Package |
|---|---|
| `SerenityRest` (`given()`, `then()`, `lastResponse()`, `reset()`) | `net.serenitybdd.rest` |
| `@Step` | `net.serenitybdd.annotations` |
| `@Steps` | `net.serenitybdd.annotations` |
| `SerenityJUnit5Extension` | `net.serenitybdd.junit5` |
| `ScenarioSteps` (optional base class, not needed) | `net.thucydides.core.steps` |

## The pattern

1. **A step library**: a plain class whose methods are annotated `@Step("business wording")`. The REST calls go inside the methods, using `SerenityRest.given()...when().get(..)`. Use `SerenityRest`, not `io.restassured.RestAssured`: it is the same API, but Serenity records every request and response in the report.
2. **The test** declares `@Steps BookshopApi bookshop;` (Serenity creates the library) and reads like a story: `bookshop.listTheBooks(); bookshop.responseShouldHaveStatus(200);`.
3. **Checks go in `@Step` methods too**, using `SerenityRest.then().statusCode(..)` and `.body("path", matcher)`, so the report shows "The response should have status 200".

`SerenityRest.then()` checks the last response of the current thread. The base URI is not remembered between calls unless you keep it in the step library (as the example does) or set `SerenityRest`/`RestAssured.baseURI`.

## Mistakes models make

| Wrong | Right |
|---|---|
| `import net.thucydides.core.annotations.Step` or `...annotations.Steps` (compile error: cannot find symbol) | `net.serenitybdd.annotations.Step`, `net.serenitybdd.annotations.Steps` |
| `import io.restassured.RestAssured.given` for calls that should appear in the report | `net.serenitybdd.rest.SerenityRest.given` |
| Creating the library with `new BookshopApi()` in the test | `@Steps BookshopApi bookshop;`. With `new`, the business steps vanish from the report and only raw `GET http://...` lines remain. |
| `@Step` missing on a method | The method still runs but the report shows only the raw `GET http://...` line instead of your wording. |
| `body("total", equalTo(90.0))` or `closeTo(90.0, 0.001)` | JSON numbers with a decimal point come back as `Float`, so a `Double` matcher fails (`Expected: <90.0>`, `Expected: a numeric value within <0.001> of <90.0>`). Use `equalTo(90.0f)`, or read the value as a double: `SerenityRest.lastResponse().jsonPath().getDouble("total")` and assert on that (AssertJ). |
| Extending `ScenarioSteps` because old guides did | Not needed. A plain class works. If you do extend it, the package is `net.thucydides.core.steps.ScenarioSteps`. |

## Wording for the living documentation

Name steps for what a person does or sees, not for the HTTP call: "Look up book number 2", "The response should show the title Clean Code", not "GET /api/books/2" or "Check JSON path title". Give each `@Test` a `@DisplayName` that states the business outcome, and the class a `@DisplayName` naming the feature (see `living-documentation.md`).

## Examples

| Style | Files |
|---|---|
| REST + step library + JUnit 5 | `rest-steps/api/*` |

## Examples

These files compile against Serenity 5.4.1 (Playwright examples: 5.3.11).

### `rest-steps/api/BookshopApi.java`

```java
package api;

import net.serenitybdd.annotations.Step;
import net.serenitybdd.rest.SerenityRest;

import static net.serenitybdd.rest.SerenityRest.given;

/** A step library: each @Step method is one line in the report, and holds the REST calls for it. */
public class BookshopApi {
    private String baseUri;

    public void usingTheServerAt(String baseUri) {
        this.baseUri = baseUri;
    }

    @Step("List the books in the catalogue")
    public void listTheBooks() {
        given().baseUri(baseUri).when().get("/api/books");
    }

    @Step("Look up book number {0}")
    public void lookUpBook(int id) {
        given().baseUri(baseUri).when().get("/api/books/" + id);
    }

    @Step("Place an order for book {0} as a signed-in reader")
    public void placeAnOrderFor(int bookId) {
        given().baseUri(baseUri)
                .header("Authorization", "Bearer abc123")
                .contentType("application/json")
                .body("{\"items\":[{\"bookId\":" + bookId + ",\"qty\":2}],\"name\":\"Ada\"}")
                .when().post("/api/orders");
    }

    @Step("Place an order without signing in")
    public void placeAnOrderWithoutSigningIn() {
        given().baseUri(baseUri)
                .contentType("application/json")
                .body("{\"items\":[{\"bookId\":1,\"qty\":1}],\"name\":\"Ada\"}")
                .when().post("/api/orders");
    }

    @Step("The response should have status {0}")
    public void responseShouldHaveStatus(int status) {
        SerenityRest.then().statusCode(status);
    }

    @Step("The response should list {0} books")
    public void responseShouldListBooks(int count) {
        SerenityRest.then().body("size()", org.hamcrest.Matchers.equalTo(count));
    }

    @Step("The response should show the title {0}")
    public void responseShouldShowTitle(String title) {
        SerenityRest.then().body("title", org.hamcrest.Matchers.equalTo(title));
    }

    @Step("The response should show the error {0}")
    public void responseShouldShowError(String message) {
        SerenityRest.then().body("error", org.hamcrest.Matchers.equalTo(message));
    }

    @Step("The order total should be {0}")
    public void orderTotalShouldBe(double total) {
        SerenityRest.then().body("total", org.hamcrest.Matchers.equalTo((float) total));
    }
}
```

### `rest-steps/api/BookshopApiTest.java`

```java
package api;

import net.serenitybdd.annotations.Steps;
import net.serenitybdd.junit5.SerenityJUnit5Extension;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterAll;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeAll;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.DisplayName;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;

@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)
@DisplayName("Browsing the book catalogue")
class BookshopApiTest {

    static final BookshopServer server = new BookshopServer();
    static int port;

    @Steps
    BookshopApi bookshop;

    @BeforeAll
    static void startServer() throws Exception {
        port = server.start();
    }

    @AfterAll
    static void stopServer() {
        server.stop();
    }

    @BeforeEach
    void pointAtTheServer() {
        bookshop.usingTheServerAt("http://localhost:" + port);
    }

    @Test
    @DisplayName("A shopper sees the catalogue and finds Clean Code by its number")
    void shopperFindsABook() {
        bookshop.listTheBooks();
        bookshop.responseShouldHaveStatus(200);
        bookshop.responseShouldListBooks(2);

        bookshop.lookUpBook(2);
        bookshop.responseShouldShowTitle("Clean Code");
    }

    @Test
    @DisplayName("A shopper who asks for a book that does not exist is told so")
    void unknownBook() {
        bookshop.lookUpBook(99);
        bookshop.responseShouldHaveStatus(404);
        bookshop.responseShouldShowError("Book not found");
    }

    @Test
    @DisplayName("A signed-in reader can place an order, and an anonymous visitor cannot")
    void ordering() {
        bookshop.placeAnOrderFor(1);
        bookshop.responseShouldHaveStatus(201);
        bookshop.orderTotalShouldBe(90.0);

        bookshop.placeAnOrderWithoutSigningIn();
        bookshop.responseShouldHaveStatus(401);
        bookshop.responseShouldShowError("Authentication required");
    }
}
```

### `rest-steps/api/BookshopServer.java`

```java
package api;

import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.net.InetSocketAddress;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;

/** A tiny stand-in for the application under test, so the example runs without a network. */
public class BookshopServer {
    private HttpServer server;

    public int start() throws IOException {
        server = HttpServer.create(new InetSocketAddress("localhost", 0), 0);
        server.createContext("/api/books", exchange -> {
            String path = exchange.getRequestURI().getPath();
            int status = 200;
            String body;
            if (path.equals("/api/books")) {
                body = "[{\"id\":1,\"title\":\"Fluent Python\",\"price\":45.0},{\"id\":2,\"title\":\"Clean Code\",\"price\":33.5}]";
            } else if (path.equals("/api/books/2")) {
                body = "{\"id\":2,\"title\":\"Clean Code\",\"price\":33.5}";
            } else {
                status = 404;
                body = "{\"error\":\"Book not found\"}";
            }
            byte[] bytes = body.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
            exchange.getResponseHeaders().add("Content-Type", "application/json");
            exchange.sendResponseHeaders(status, bytes.length);
            exchange.getResponseBody().write(bytes);
            exchange.close();
        });
        server.createContext("/api/orders", exchange -> {
            boolean signedIn = "Bearer abc123".equals(exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("Authorization"));
            int status = signedIn ? 201 : 401;
            String body = signedIn ? "{\"id\":\"ORD-1001\",\"total\":90.0,\"status\":\"PLACED\"}" : "{\"error\":\"Authentication required\"}";
            byte[] bytes = body.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
            exchange.getResponseHeaders().add("Content-Type", "application/json");
            exchange.sendResponseHeaders(status, bytes.length);
            exchange.getResponseBody().write(bytes);
            exchange.close();
        });
        server.start();
        return server.getAddress().getPort();
    }

    public void stop() {
        server.stop(0);
    }
}
```

# Configuration: serenity.conf, Properties and Environments

Verified against Serenity **5.4.1**. The behaviour described here was run against the example at the end of the page.

## 1. Where configuration comes from

| Source | Where | Read? |
|---|---|---|
| `serenity.conf` (HOCON) | `src/test/resources/` (on the classpath) | yes |
| `serenity.conf` | project root | **no, ignored** |
| `serenity.properties` | project root | yes |
| `serenity.properties` | `src/test/resources/` | yes |
| System properties | `-Dkey=value` on the Maven command line | yes, override the files |

What wins:

- A `-D` option wins over both files (`-Dwebdriver.base.url=...` replaced the value in the file).
- `serenity.properties` in the **project root** wins over `serenity.conf` in `src/test/resources`.
- `serenity.conf` wins over a `serenity.properties` that is also in `src/test/resources`.
- OS environment variables (`SERENITY_PROJECT_NAME=...`) did **not** set `serenity.project.name`.

`thucydides.*` and `serenity.*` are synonyms: `thucydides.project.name = "x"` in either file sets the project name. Prefer `serenity.*`.

After deleting or moving a configuration file, run `mvn clean ...`: Maven leaves the old copy in `target/test-classes`, so a deleted `serenity.conf` is still read (checked: the old value was still used without `clean`).

## 2. `serenity.conf`

HOCON. Nested and dotted forms mean the same:

```hocon
serenity {
  project.name = "My project"
  take.screenshots = FOR_FAILURES
}
webdriver {
  base.url = "https://example.com"
}
headless.mode = true
```

The full example, with environments, is `config/resources/serenity.conf`.

## 3. Environments

```hocon
environments {
  default { app.url = "https://dev.example.com"
            db.name = "dev" }
  staging { app.url = "https://staging.example.com" }
  all     { company = "Acme" }
}
```

Pick one with `-Denvironment=staging`.

- With no `environment`, the `default` block applies. With `-Denvironment=staging`, `staging` applies and values it does not define fall back to `default` (`db.name` stayed `dev`).
- `all` applies in every environment.
- **Your own keys inside `environments { }` are NOT visible as plain properties.** `environmentVariables.getProperty("app.url")` returns **null**, in every environment. Read them through `EnvironmentSpecificConfiguration` (next section). This is the usual cause of "I get null when I read a value from serenity.conf".
- **Serenity's own keys inside `environments { }` do work** and override the top-level value: `webdriver.base.url` and `serenity.project.name` inside `environments { staging { } }` took effect with `-Denvironment=staging`. Values in `default` override the top-level value too.
- Command-line override of a value in `environments`: use the full name, `-Denvironments.staging.app.url=https://...`. A plain `-Dapp.url=...` did **not** override it.

## 4. Reading values in code

```java
EnvironmentVariables env = SystemEnvironmentVariables.currentEnvironmentVariables();   // net.thucydides.model.environment
String name = ThucydidesSystemProperty.SERENITY_PROJECT_NAME.from(env);                 // net.thucydides.model
String url  = EnvironmentSpecificConfiguration.from(env).getOptionalProperty("app.url").orElse("none"); // net.serenitybdd.model.environment
```

- Works anywhere, including static code and static initialisers. `Serenity.environmentVariables()` (`net.serenitybdd.core.Serenity`) returns the same kind of object.
- In a step library (a class with `@Step` methods used through `@Steps`), declare a field `EnvironmentVariables environmentVariables;` (type `net.thucydides.model.util.EnvironmentVariables`): Serenity injects it.
- Built-in keys: `ThucydidesSystemProperty.X.from(env)` (also `integerFrom`, `booleanFrom`, `isDefinedIn`) or `env.getProperty("webdriver.base.url")`.
- Your own keys outside `environments { }` can be read with `env.getProperty("my.key")`.

## 5. Common keys

All of these exist in `ThucydidesSystemProperty` (checked). Meanings are from the Serenity documentation, except where marked *(run)*.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `webdriver.driver` | Which browser to run in (`chrome`, `firefox`, `edge`, `safari`, ...). An unknown name fails with `Unsupported browser type` *(run)*. |
| `webdriver.base.url` | The default starting URL; base for relative paths. Read back *(run)*. |
| `headless.mode` | Headless Chrome, Firefox or Edge. `true` added Chrome's `--headless` arguments *(run)*. |
| `webdriver.chrome.driver` | Path to a chromedriver binary. Only set it if you really supply one; a missing file is an error *(run)*. |
| `webdriver.autodownload` | `false` stops Serenity downloading driver binaries. |
| `webdriver.remote.url`, `webdriver.remote.driver` | The URL of a Selenium Grid or cloud hub, and the driver to use there. |
| `webdriver.timeouts.implicitlywait` | How long the driver waits for elements to appear, in milliseconds. |
| `webdriver.wait.for.timeout` | How long fluent waits wait, in milliseconds. |
| `serenity.project.name` | The name shown on reports. Read back *(run)*. |
| `serenity.outputDirectory` | Where reports go (default `target/site/serenity`). |
| `serenity.take.screenshots` | `FOR_EACH_ACTION`, `BEFORE_AND_AFTER_EACH_STEP`, `AFTER_EACH_STEP`, `FOR_FAILURES` or `DISABLED`. On a passing test `DISABLED` and `FOR_FAILURES` stored no screenshots; the other values, and not setting it, stored some *(run)*. |
| `serenity.browser.width`, `serenity.browser.height` | Browser window size. |
| `serenity.restart.browser.frequency` | Start a new browser every N rows in data-driven tests. |
| `serenity.reports.show.step.details` | Show a breakdown of steps by result in report tables. |

Do not invent keys. If a key is not in the Serenity documentation or `ThucydidesSystemProperty`, it is probably ignored without any message.

## 6. Setting values from the build

- **Maven, one run:** `mvn verify -Denvironment=staging -Dwebdriver.driver=firefox`.
- **Maven, fixed in the pom:** put them in the test plugin's `<systemPropertyVariables>`. (A pom property such as `${cucumber.filter.tags}` can feed it.)
- **Gradle:** `gradle test -Denvironment=staging` does **not** reach the tests unless `build.gradle` forwards it, as for the Cucumber options (see the Cucumber page): a filtered selection inside `test { }`, such as `systemProperties System.properties.findAll { k, v -> k.toString().startsWith('serenity.') || k == 'environment' }`.

## 7. Mistakes

| Wrong | Right |
|---|---|
| `serenity.conf` in the project root | `src/test/resources/serenity.conf` |
| Reading `app.url` with `env.getProperty` when it is defined under `environments { }` | `EnvironmentSpecificConfiguration.from(env).getOptionalProperty("app.url")` |
| `-Dapp.url=...` to override a value defined under `environments { staging { } }` | `-Denvironments.staging.app.url=...` |
| An old `serenity.properties` in the project root silently beating `serenity.conf` | Keep one file, or remember that the root properties file wins |
| Setting a key through an OS environment variable | Use `-D`, the file, or the build tool's system property settings |
| Hard-coding `webdriver.chrome.driver` to a path on one machine | Leave it unset (see Troubleshooting) |

## 8. Not covered

Cloud and grid capabilities (`serenity.driver.capabilities`, `webdriver.capabilities.*`), proxies, Appium settings, the `drivers { os { } }` blocks, requirements and report customisation keys, and `.serenity` files in a user home directory. See the documentation page of Serenity properties.

## Examples

These files compile against Serenity 5.4.1 (Playwright examples: 5.3.11).

### `config/cfg/ConfigReader.java`

```java
package cfg;

import net.serenitybdd.model.environment.EnvironmentSpecificConfiguration;
import net.thucydides.model.util.EnvironmentVariables;

/** A step library. Serenity injects the EnvironmentVariables field. */
public class ConfigReader {

    EnvironmentVariables environmentVariables;

    public String appUrl() {
        return EnvironmentSpecificConfiguration.from(environmentVariables).getOptionalProperty("app.url").orElse("<none>");
    }

    public boolean injected() {
        return environmentVariables != null;
    }
}
```

### `config/cfg/ConfigurationTest.java`

```java
package cfg;

import net.serenitybdd.annotations.Steps;
import net.serenitybdd.core.Serenity;
import net.serenitybdd.junit5.SerenityJUnit5Extension;
import net.serenitybdd.model.environment.EnvironmentSpecificConfiguration;
import net.thucydides.model.ThucydidesSystemProperty;
import net.thucydides.model.environment.SystemEnvironmentVariables;
import net.thucydides.model.util.EnvironmentVariables;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)
class ConfigurationTest {

    @Steps
    ConfigReader reader;

    @Test
    void readsValuesFromSerenityConf() {
        // Anywhere in the code, including a static context:
        EnvironmentVariables env = SystemEnvironmentVariables.currentEnvironmentVariables();
        EnvironmentSpecificConfiguration environmentConfig = EnvironmentSpecificConfiguration.from(env);

        // Plain keys: through the property enum, or by name
        System.out.println("CFG base.url=" + ThucydidesSystemProperty.WEBDRIVER_BASE_URL.from(env));
        System.out.println("CFG project.name=" + ThucydidesSystemProperty.SERENITY_PROJECT_NAME.from(env));
        System.out.println("CFG by-name=" + env.getProperty("webdriver.base.url"));
        System.out.println("CFG serenity-facade=" + Serenity.environmentVariables().getProperty("webdriver.base.url"));

        System.out.println("CFG my.setting=" + env.getProperty("my.setting"));

        // Keys under environments { }: ONLY through EnvironmentSpecificConfiguration
        System.out.println("CFG plain app.url=" + env.getProperty("app.url"));
        System.out.println("CFG specific app.url=" + environmentConfig.getOptionalProperty("app.url").orElse("<none>"));
        System.out.println("CFG specific db.name=" + environmentConfig.getOptionalProperty("db.name").orElse("<none>"));
        System.out.println("CFG specific company=" + environmentConfig.getOptionalProperty("company").orElse("<none>"));
        System.out.println("CFG injected=" + reader.injected() + " " + reader.appUrl());

        assertThat(ThucydidesSystemProperty.SERENITY_PROJECT_NAME.from(env)).isNotBlank();
        assertThat(reader.injected()).isTrue();
    }
}
```

### `config/resources/serenity.conf`

```hocon

  }
```

# Project Setup: Dependencies and Configuration

Verified against Serenity **5.4.1**. The dependency sets, JUnit BOM and report plugin were run end to end (`mvn clean verify` ran the examples and produced the report). The `serenity.conf` snippet follows the project's own samples but was not run.

Use one Serenity version for every `net.serenity-bdd` artifact (a `serenity.version` property). Java 17+. Playwright modules are published up to 5.3.11, so a Playwright project may need `serenity.version` 5.3.11 for those artifacts; check Maven Central for the latest before pinning.

## Dependencies by style (all `test` scope)

| Style | `net.serenity-bdd` artifacts | Other |
|---|---|---|
| Page Objects + Selenium | `serenity-core`, `serenity-junit5` | `org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter`, `org.assertj:assertj-core` |
| Page Objects + Playwright | `serenity-core`, `serenity-junit5`, `serenity-playwright` | + `com.microsoft.playwright:playwright` |
| Screenplay + Selenium | `serenity-core`, `serenity-junit5`, `serenity-screenplay`, `serenity-screenplay-webdriver`, `serenity-ensure` | JUnit Jupiter, AssertJ |
| Screenplay + Playwright | `serenity-core`, `serenity-junit5`, `serenity-screenplay`, `serenity-screenplay-playwright`, `serenity-playwright` | JUnit Jupiter, `com.microsoft.playwright:playwright` |
| Screenplay + REST | `serenity-core`, `serenity-junit5`, `serenity-screenplay`, `serenity-screenplay-rest`, `serenity-rest-assured`, `serenity-ensure` | JUnit Jupiter |
| Cucumber (+ Screenplay) | the Screenplay web set above, plus `serenity-cucumber` | `io.cucumber:cucumber-java`, `io.cucumber:cucumber-junit-platform-engine`, `org.junit.platform:junit-platform-suite` |

Serenity 5.4.1 itself depends on **JUnit 6.1.3** (`serenity-junit5`) and **Cucumber 8.0.4** (`serenity-cucumber`). Don't pin older JUnit or Cucumber versions: mixed JUnit versions fail at run time with "conflicting versions" errors, even though the code compiles. Import the JUnit BOM so every JUnit artifact (including `junit-platform-suite` and the engine that `cucumber-junit-platform-engine` brings in) has the same version:

```xml
<dependencyManagement>
  <dependencies>
    <dependency><groupId>org.junit</groupId><artifactId>junit-bom</artifactId><version>6.1.3</version><type>pom</type><scope>import</scope></dependency>
  </dependencies>
</dependencyManagement>
```

Then list `junit-jupiter` and `junit-platform-suite` without versions, and use Cucumber 8.0.4 for `cucumber-java` and `cucumber-junit-platform-engine`. Other versions in the harness: Playwright 1.52.0, AssertJ 3.27.7. Add `org.slf4j:slf4j-simple` to silence logging warnings.

## Build and reports

```xml
<plugin><groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId><artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId><version>3.5.1</version></plugin>
<plugin><groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId><artifactId>maven-failsafe-plugin</artifactId><version>3.5.1</version></plugin>
<plugin>
  <groupId>net.serenity-bdd.maven.plugins</groupId>
  <artifactId>serenity-maven-plugin</artifactId>
  <version>${serenity.version}</version>
  <executions>
    <execution><id>serenity-reports</id><phase>post-integration-test</phase><goals><goal>aggregate</goal></goals></execution>
  </executions>
</plugin>
```

- Compile only: `mvn test-compile` (fast, use it to check generated code).
- Run and build the report: `mvn clean verify`. The report is in `target/site/serenity/index.html`.
- Name test classes so surefire/failsafe pick them up (`*Test`, or `*IT` for failsafe); a Cucumber runner is a JUnit Platform `@Suite` class.

## `src/test/resources/serenity.conf` (HOCON)

```hocon
serenity {
  project.name = "My project"
  take.screenshots = FOR_FAILURES      # FOR_EACH_ACTION, BEFORE_AND_AFTER_EACH_STEP, DISABLED
}
headless.mode = true
webdriver.base.url = "https://example.com"
environments {
  default { base.url = "https://example.com" }
}
```

`serenity.*` and `thucydides.*` keys are synonyms; prefer `serenity.*`. Don't invent keys: check `docs/reference` on https://serenity-bdd.github.io or `ThucydidesSystemProperty` in `serenity-model`.

These files compile against Serenity 5.4.1 (Playwright examples: 5.3.11).

# Troubleshooting by Symptom

Verified against Serenity **5.4.1** (Playwright modules: **5.3.11**). Each entry was reproduced in a test project and its fix was run.

How to use this page: find the message you see (the text is quoted from the real output), read the cause, apply the fix, and run the build again. If nothing here matches, read the first `Caused by:` and the first `[ERROR]` line in the Maven output, not the last.

## Where to look first

- Serenity writes one JSON file per test to `target/site/serenity/` as the tests run. If the HTML report is missing, these files still show what happened.
- The line `Results: N tests | ...` in the Maven output (from the Serenity Maven plugin) tells you how many tests Serenity saw.
- `mvn -q test-compile` separates compile errors from run-time ones.

## The build fails or does nothing

### "The wrapped NoClassDefFoundError is likely caused by the versions of JUnit jars ... not being properly aligned"

```
The following conflicting versions were detected:
- org.junit.jupiter.api: 6.1.3
- org.junit.platform.suite.api: 1.12.2 ...
```

- **Cause:** the pom pins `junit-jupiter`, `junit-platform-suite` or another JUnit artifact to a version other than the one Serenity brings. Serenity 5.4.1 depends on **JUnit 6.1.3**. The code compiles; the tests fail when they start.
- **Fix:** remove the pinned JUnit versions and import the JUnit BOM so all JUnit artifacts match:

```xml
<dependencyManagement>
  <dependencies>
    <dependency><groupId>org.junit</groupId><artifactId>junit-bom</artifactId><version>6.1.3</version><type>pom</type><scope>import</scope></dependency>
  </dependencies>
</dependencyManagement>
```

List `junit-jupiter` and `junit-platform-suite` without versions.

### `java.lang.AbstractMethodError: Receiver class io.cucumber.junit.platform.engine.CucumberConfiguration does not define or inherit an implementation of the resolved method 'abstract ... getGlueDiscoveryRequest()'`

- **Cause:** `cucumber-java` or `cucumber-junit-platform-engine` is pinned to a version that does not match the Cucumber that `serenity-cucumber` brings (8.0.4 for Serenity 5.4.1; 7.34.2 for 5.3.11). Reproduced with 7.31.0.
- **Fix:** use the version Serenity brings (check with `mvn dependency:tree -Dincludes=io.cucumber`), or leave the Cucumber versions out.

### `Failed to transform configuration parameter with key 'cucumber.plugin' and initial value 'io.cucumber.core.plugin.SerenityReporterParallel,pretty'`

- **Cause:** the Serenity plugin class is named with the wrong package.
- **Fix:** `@ConfigurationParameter(key = PLUGIN_PROPERTY_NAME, value = "net.serenitybdd.cucumber.core.plugin.SerenityReporterParallel,pretty")`.

### The build succeeds but `Results: 0 tests | 0 passed | ...`, no Cucumber scenarios ran, and the report is empty

```
[INFO]   - Results: 0 tests | 0 passed | 0 failed | 0 errors | 0 compromised | 0 pending | 0 aborted
```

- **Cause:** Maven's test plugin only runs classes whose names match its default patterns (`*Test`, `*Tests`, `Test*`, `*TestCase`). A Cucumber `@Suite` class called, for example, `CucumberSuite` or `CucumberTestSuite` is skipped without any warning. Reproduced with `CucumberSuite`.
- **Fix:** name the runner `RunCucumberTests` (or any name ending in `Test` or `Tests`), or add the name to `<includes>` in the surefire plugin configuration.

## The report is missing or wrong

### Tests failed, and there is no `target/site/serenity/index.html`

- **Cause:** the report is built by the Serenity Maven plugin in the `post-integration-test` phase, which Maven never reaches when tests fail. The per-test JSON files exist, but no HTML. Reproduced: after a failing scenario, `mvn verify` printed `There are test failures`, and `index.html` was absent.
- **Fix:** either run the report goal after the failed build:

```
mvn net.serenity-bdd.maven.plugins:serenity-maven-plugin:5.4.1:aggregate
```

(this produced `index.html`), or let the build continue past test failures with `-Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=true` (then the exit code is 0 even when tests fail, so a CI job must check results another way). To find out what failed without any report, read the JSON files: `python3 scripts/results.py target/site/serenity` (see `test-results.md`).

### `Conflicting module versions. Module [groovy-xml is loaded in version 4.0.29 and you are trying to load version 3.0.9` / `Could not initialize class io.restassured.RestAssured`

- **Cause:** the pom pins REST-assured (`io.rest-assured:*`) or Groovy (`org.codehaus.groovy:groovy*`, Groovy 3) versions left over from an older Serenity. Serenity 5.4.1's REST support uses Groovy 4. Reproduced with REST-assured 4.5.1 and Groovy 3.0.9.
- **Fix:** delete those dependencies and let `serenity-rest-assured` bring its own. Seen when upgrading a real Serenity 2.4 project, which then passed 3 of 3 scenarios.

### The report shows more tests, or old failures, than the run had

- **Cause:** Serenity counts every outcome file in `target/site/serenity`, including ones left by earlier runs. Reproduced: after a full run (5 scenarios), a run filtered to 1 scenario, without cleaning, reported `Results: 5 tests`; after the directory was deleted it reported 1 (the verification script in the serenity-core repository (`docs/ai/skill`), case `stale-outcomes-counted`).
- **Fix:** start from a clean directory: `mvn clean verify`, or delete `target/site/serenity` (Gradle: `gradle clean test`, whose `clean` also clears it).

### "No BaseStepListener has been registered - are you running your test using the Serenity runners?"

```
java.lang.NullPointerException: No BaseStepListener has been registered - are you running your test using the Serenity runners?
```

- **Cause:** code that uses Serenity's reporting or Screenplay (for example `Serenity.recordReportData()`, an actor performing a task) runs outside a Serenity-managed test. In Cucumber the usual reason is that the Serenity plugin is not in the runner's `PLUGIN_PROPERTY_NAME`. Reproduced by removing the plugin.
- **Fix:** in Cucumber, add `net.serenitybdd.cucumber.core.plugin.SerenityReporterParallel` to the plugins. In a JUnit 5 test, add `@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)`.

### A value defined in `serenity.conf` reads as `null`

- **Cause (two common ones):** (1) the value is under `environments { }`, and `environmentVariables.getProperty("app.url")` never returns those; (2) the file is not where Serenity looks: `serenity.conf` is read from `src/test/resources`, not the project root. Reproduced both (the verification script in the serenity-core repository (`docs/ai/skill`)).
- **Fix:** (1) `EnvironmentSpecificConfiguration.from(env).getOptionalProperty("app.url")`; (2) move the file to `src/test/resources/serenity.conf` and run `mvn clean`.

### Filtering by tag does nothing under Gradle: all scenarios still run

- **Cause:** Gradle does not pass `-D` options on the command line to the tests' JVM, so `gradle test -Dcucumber.filter.tags=@smoke` is ignored. Reproduced: 4 outcomes with the option, unchanged, and 1 once the build forwarded it.
- **Fix:** forward the option in `build.gradle`, as in the Cucumber page: `systemProperties System.properties.findAll { k, v -> k.toString().startsWith('cucumber.') }` inside `test { }`.

## The browser

### `NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "org.openqa.selenium.WebDriver.get(String)" because "this.driver" is null`

- **Cause:** a `@Managed WebDriver driver;` field in a **step library** (or any class other than the test class). `@Managed` only fills the field in the test class; elsewhere it stays null. Reproduced in a step library.
- **Fix:** extend `net.serenitybdd.core.steps.UIInteractionSteps` and use `getDriver()` (or use a page object, which gets the driver itself). Keep `@Managed` for the test class.

### `DriverConfigurationError: Unsupported browser type: chromee. Did you mean firefox?`

- **Cause:** `webdriver.driver` (system property or `serenity.conf`) names a browser Serenity does not know. Reproduced with a misspelling.
- **Fix:** use a supported name: `chrome`, `firefox`, `edge`, `safari`, `iexplorer`, `appium`, `remote`, ... (in this case the message guessed `firefox` for a misspelt `chrome`, so read the list rather than trusting the suggestion).

### `DriverConfigurationError: After several attempts, could not instantiate new WebDriver instance of type class org.openqa.selenium.chrome.ChromeDriver (Unable to obtain: chromedriver, error chromedriver must exist: /no/such/chromedriver`

- **Cause:** `webdriver.chrome.driver` points to a file that does not exist (a stale path from another machine or an old setup).
- **Also seen as:** `chromedriver must be executable: src/test/resources/webdriver/mac/chromedriver`, from an old `drivers { mac { webdriver.chrome.driver = "..." } }` block with a bundled binary (found upgrading a real Serenity 2.1 project; removing the block let Chrome start).
- **Fix:** remove the property so Selenium downloads or finds a matching driver by itself, or set it to a real path. Do not commit machine-specific absolute paths; if a driver must be supplied, see the OS-specific `drivers` settings in the driver configuration docs.

### `no such element: Unable to locate element: {"method":"xpath","selector":"input.new-todo"}` (Screenplay with Selenium)

- **Cause:** `Target.the(..).locatedBy("input.new-todo")`. Serenity reads the string as XPath when it compiles as an XPath expression, and `input.new-todo` does (a name test). So the element is searched as XPath and not found. `.new-todo`, `#id` and `[data-x=y]` are read as CSS.
- **Fix:** `Target.the(..).located(By.cssSelector("input.new-todo"))`, or a CSS selector that starts with `.`, `#` or `[`.

### `NoClassDefFoundError: io/cucumber/core/eventbus/EventBus` (and similar) after raising the Serenity version

- **Cause:** the project still pins an older Cucumber (4.x) and excludes `cucumber-core` from Serenity, as old starter projects did. Seen upgrading a real Serenity 2.1 project; not reproduced in the test projects here. After the pin and the exclusion were replaced by Cucumber 8.0.4 the project built; remember `mvn clean`, because old compiled classes can hide the next error (see the upgrading reference).
- **Fix:** use the Cucumber version Serenity brings (8.0.4 for 5.4.1) and remove the exclusion.

## Not reproduced here

These come up often in public questions. They are not covered by a tested fix, so use the driver configuration and Maven documentation, and do not rely on advice you cannot check:

- `Chrome failed to start: exited normally` / `session not created` after a Chrome update, `DevToolsActivePort file doesn't exist`, and browser start-up problems inside Docker or on Jenkins (they depend on the machine, user and container).
- Dependency convergence errors and `Could not resolve dependencies` (they depend on the project's other dependencies).
- `NoClassDefFoundError` after upgrading from Serenity 3 to 4 (for example `net.thucydides.model.util.EnvironmentVariables`): classes moved between packages. The upgrade guide in the documentation lists them.
- Slow report aggregation, wrong counts and reports from parallel runs.

These files compile against Serenity 5.4.1 (Playwright examples: 5.3.11).

# Upgrading to Serenity 5 and Recognising Old Code

Verified against Serenity **5.4.1**. The class counts come from the released jars, and the recipe was applied to five real projects.

## 1. What changed, by release

| Coming from | Java needed | What you must change |
|---|---|---|
| 4.x (tested: 4.2.34) | Java **17** (4.x classes are Java 11, 5.x classes are Java 17) | Versions only. All 1,587 public classes in the core, model, JUnit, Screenplay (including WebDriver and REST), REST-assured, Cucumber and Ensure jars have the same name and package in 5.4.1. A 4.2.8 project compiled with only a version bump. Align the JUnit and Cucumber versions with Serenity's (section 3). |
| 3.x (tested: 3.9.8) | Java 17 (3.x classes are Java 8) | Version bump, **511 of 1,574 classes moved** (section 2), the artifact changes in section 3, and the fixes for removed API found by the compiler. |
| 2.x | Java 17 | The same as 3.x, plus renamed Cucumber artifacts. |

Serenity 5.4.1 depends on **JUnit 6.1.3** and **Cucumber 8.0.4** (`../references/project-setup.md`).

## 2. Classes that moved (3.x to 5.x)

Of the 1,574 public classes in the 3.9.8 jars: 1,051 are unchanged, 511 moved to exactly one new place, 7 have a same-named class in more than one place, 5 are gone. Many `net.thucydides` packages are still correct (for example `net.thucydides.core.steps.ScenarioSteps`, `net.thucydides.core.pages.Pages`, and the 47 classes in `net.thucydides.core.steps` that did not move): only the classes in the table moved. All of `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.*`, `net.serenitybdd.core.pages`, `net.serenitybdd.junit.runners` and `net.thucydides.core.webdriver` (except two classes) kept their packages.

The annotations are the ones most code touches: `Step`, `Steps`, `Managed`, `DefaultUrl`, `Title`, `Narrative`, `Pending`, `WithTag`, `Issue` and the rest of `net.thucydides.core.annotations` are now in **`net.serenitybdd.annotations`**. `EnvironmentVariables` is in `net.thucydides.model.util`; `EnvironmentSpecificConfiguration` is in `net.serenitybdd.model.environment`.

Ambiguous: `Story` (`net.serenitybdd.annotations.Story` for the annotation, `net.thucydides.model.domain.Story` for the model class), `CastMember` (`net.serenitybdd.screenplay.annotations.CastMember` for Screenplay), `Release`, `PathElements` and `TagParser`: decide by what the code uses it for. Gone: the WebDriverManager integration classes (`WebDriverManagerSetup`, `WebDriverManagerEnhancer`, `DefaultWebDriverManagerEnhancer`; drivers are found by Selenium itself now), `MergedRequirementList` and `RecordStepResultEvent`.

**Rewriting imports automatically:** the `fix_imports.py` script in the serenity-core repository (`docs/ai/skill/upgrade-checks`) rewrites every class in the table (imports, fully qualified names, wildcard imports) and lists the ambiguous and removed classes it found, for a person to decide.

## 3. The upgrade recipe

Each step was needed by at least one of the five tested projects.

1. **Java 17** or later for the build and the tests.
2. **Set the Serenity version** everywhere it appears (`serenity.version`, the Maven plugin version, `serenity.cucumber.version`).
3. **Artifact names.** `serenity-cucumber4`, `serenity-cucumber5` and `serenity-cucumber6` stopped at 2.1.2, 2.2.6 and 2.6.0: use **`serenity-cucumber`**. The JUnit 4 runner (`net.serenitybdd.junit.runners.SerenityRunner`) lives in **`serenity-junit`**, which a 3.x project got through `serenity-core`: add it, with JUnit 4.13.2, if you keep JUnit 4 tests. `serenity-jbehave` has no 5.x release (its last version is 1.46.0): JBehave stories need migrating to Cucumber first. Check any other `serenity-*` artifact on Maven Central before relying on it.
4. **Remove versions that Serenity manages.** Pins that were right for the old Serenity break the new one at run time, not at compile time:
   - Cucumber: a pinned `cucumber-java`, `cucumber-junit` or an `<exclusion>` of `cucumber-core` gives `NoClassDefFoundError: io/cucumber/core/eventbus/EventBus` (a project with Cucumber 4.8.1 and the exclusion). Use 8.0.4, or none, and delete the exclusion.
   - REST-assured and Groovy: pinned `io.rest-assured:*` and `org.codehaus.groovy:groovy*` (Groovy 3) give `Conflicting module versions. Module [groovy-xml is loaded in version 3.0.6 and you are trying to load version 4.0.29`. Delete them; `serenity-rest-assured` brings the right ones.
   - JUnit: see the troubleshooting reference ("conflicting versions"); import the JUnit BOM.
5. **Imports.** Run `fix_imports.py` (section 2).
6. **Configuration clean-up** (`../references/configuration.md`):
   - Delete a `drivers { mac { webdriver.chrome.driver = "src/test/resources/webdriver/..." } }` block of bundled driver binaries. A 2020 chromedriver cannot drive a current Chrome, and the symptom is `Could not instantiate class org.openqa.selenium.chrome.ChromeDriver ... chromedriver must be executable`. With the block removed, Chrome started.
   - `screenshooter=shutterbug` needs the separate `serenity-shutterbug` artifact; otherwise the test fails with `Unable to instantiate screen shooter net.serenitybdd.screenshots.shutterbug.ShutterbugScreenShooter`. Delete the line (default screenshots) or add the artifact.
7. **Compile from clean:** `mvn clean test-compile`. Without `clean`, Maven keeps classes compiled against the old libraries: a `cucumber.api.CucumberOptions` import compiled for as long as the stale class file existed, and the runner then silently ran **0 scenarios**.
8. **Fix removed or renamed API** (the compiler lists it). Found in the tested projects: `InputField.called("x")` and `PageElement.called("x")` (gone by 3.9.8) became `InputField.withNameOrId("x")` and `PageElement.withNameOrId("x")`. `cucumber.api.CucumberOptions` became `io.cucumber.junit.CucumberOptions`, and `cucumber.api.java.en.*` became `io.cucumber.java.en.*` (the `cucumber.api` package does not exist in Cucumber 8).
9. **Run the tests.** Failures that remain may belong to the application under test: three of the five old projects' remaining failures were a changed page (a search box and a to-do input that no longer exist).

## 4. Evidence: five real projects

| Project (Serenity version) | Result |
|---|---|
| REST starter with Cucumber (2.4.51) | Version, `serenity-cucumber6` to `serenity-cucumber`, 2 class references rewritten, REST-assured and Groovy pins removed: **3 of 3 scenarios pass**. |
| Cucumber 4 starter (2.1.12) | Version, 4 class references rewritten, Cucumber 4.8.1 and the exclusion replaced by 8.0.4, runner import fixed, bundled drivers removed: compiles and the 4 scenarios run in Chrome; they fail on the DuckDuckGo search box, which has changed. |
| Screenplay with JUnit 4 and Cucumber, todo app (3.3.0) | Version, `serenity-junit` added, 6 class references rewritten: compiles; 4 of 10 scenarios pass, 6 fail on a to-do input that one of the sample apps no longer has. |
| Screenplay quickstart (3.0.2) | Compiles after `called` became `withNameOrId`; the run needed the `shutterbug` line removed, then fails on Wikipedia's changed search box (`element not interactable`). |
| Toolshop (4.2.8) | Compiles with only the version bump. Its tests were not run. |

## 5. JUnit 4 and the old Cucumber runner still work

You do not have to move to JUnit 5. With `serenity-junit` and JUnit 4.13.2, `@RunWith(SerenityRunner.class)` with `@Steps` ran on 5.4.1 (1 test passed), and so did `@RunWith(CucumberWithSerenity.class)` with `@CucumberOptions(features = ..., glue = ...)` from `io.cucumber.junit` (3 scenarios passed). Use the JUnit 5 extension and the JUnit Platform suite for new code (`../references/cucumber.md`); do not rewrite a working JUnit 4 suite only to follow it. Keep one style per project.

## 6. Recognising old code in generated or copied examples

| Old | Current |
|---|---|
| `import net.thucydides.core.annotations.{Step,Steps,Managed,DefaultUrl,...}` | `net.serenitybdd.annotations.*` |
| `net.thucydides.core.util.EnvironmentVariables` | `net.thucydides.model.util.EnvironmentVariables` |
| `net.serenitybdd.core.environment.EnvironmentSpecificConfiguration` | `net.serenitybdd.model.environment.EnvironmentSpecificConfiguration` |
| `serenity-cucumber4/5/6`, `cucumber.api.*` | `serenity-cucumber`, `io.cucumber.*` |
| `InputField.called(..)`, `PageElement.called(..)` | `InputField.withNameOrId(..)`, `PageElement.withNameOrId(..)` |
| `drivers { os { webdriver.chrome.driver = ... } }` with bundled binaries | nothing: leave driver selection to Serenity and Selenium |
| `serenity-jbehave` stories | no 5.x release: migrate to Cucumber |
| `@RunWith(SerenityRunner.class)` | still valid with `serenity-junit` and JUnit 4; for JUnit 5 use `@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)` |
| `net.thucydides.core.steps.ScenarioSteps`, `net.thucydides.core.pages.Pages` | **not old**: still in those packages |

## 7. Not covered

Gradle plugin version history, Serenity 1.x, Appium and mobile modules, the Spring, JIRA and cloud-provider modules, and Selenium 3 to 4 API changes outside Serenity's own classes.

# Reading Test Results Without the HTML Report

Verified against Serenity **5.4.1** by running a passing and a failing project: the files, the fields and the script were all checked.

An AI assistant, a script or a CI step can read the outcome of a run from files, not from the HTML report or the Maven console. Serenity writes them to `target/site/serenity/`.

## What is written, and when

| File | Written | Contains |
|---|---|---|
| `<64 hex characters>.json`, one per test | **While the tests run.** It exists after a failed build, when no HTML report was generated | The full outcome of one test: title, result, requirement path, the step tree, and the failure |
| `SERENITY-JUNIT-<same 64 hex characters>.xml`, one per test | While the tests run | The same test in standard JUnit XML, for CI tools |
| `index.html`, the other `.html` pages, `summary.txt` | **Only if the report was generated.** `mvn verify` stops at a failed test, so after a failure they are missing (see the troubleshooting page) | The HTML report; `summary.txt` has the totals as prose |
| `serenity-summary.json` | Only if the optional JSON summary report is enabled (below) | Totals and one entry per scenario |

The JSON file name is a 64-character hash. It was the same on every run of the same test, but it tells you nothing about the test, so read the `title`, `testCaseName` and `methodName` fields inside.

So after any run, including a failed one, **read `target/site/serenity/*.json`**. Do not wait for `index.html` and do not scrape it.

## The quickest way: `scripts/results.py`

The script is in the skill (`scripts/results.py`) and in the serenity-core repository at `docs/ai/skill/serenity-bdd/scripts/results.py`; copy it into the project if the skill is not installed.

```bash
python3 <skill>/scripts/results.py target/site/serenity          # totals, a line per test, details of each failure
python3 <skill>/scripts/results.py target/site/serenity --json   # the same as one JSON document
```

It prints the totals, one line per test (result, title, requirement path, outcome file), and for each failed test the failing step, the exception type and message, the first stack frame in the project's own code, and the outcome file to open for the full detail. The exit code is 1 if any test failed, errored or was compromised, and 2 if there are no outcome files. A run of more than 40 tests lists only the tests that did not pass unless you add `--all`. It reads only the JSON files, uses no dependencies, and is a different tool from `outline.py` (which judges the wording and structure of the report, not the result of the run).

When the failure is an assertion or a wait (for example Screenplay `WaitUntil` or `should(seeThat(..))`), Serenity may not mark any step as failed. The script then says so and gives the last step recorded; the stack frame names the line of your test that failed.

## The fields of an outcome file

```text
title, name          the scenario title as the report shows it
result               SUCCESS, FAILURE, ERROR, COMPROMISED, PENDING, SKIPPED, IGNORED ...
testCaseName         class name; methodName: the test method (JUnit)
userStory            { path, storyName, ... }  the requirement it belongs to (package path or feature file)
featureTag, tags     the feature and any @tags
startTime, duration  duration in milliseconds
testSource           JUnit5, Cucumber ...
testSteps            the step tree: [ { number, description, result, duration, children: [ ... ] } ]
```

For a test that did not pass, the file also has:

```text
testFailureCause     { errorType, message, stackTrace: [ { declaringClass, methodName, fileName, lineNumber } ] }
testFailureClassname the exception class
testFailureMessage   the exception message
testFailureSummary   "FAILURE;<class>;<message>;<file>"
```

and the step that failed (when one is marked) has `exception` with the same `errorType`, `message` and `stackTrace`. REST steps carry `restQuery` with `method`, `path`, `requestHeaders`, `content`, `statusCode`, `responseHeaders` and `responseBody`, which is often all that is needed to see why an API test failed. Nested steps are in `children`.

The step tree is long for big tests (every request, with its response body, is in it). Read the summary first and open one outcome file only for a test you are investigating.

## Optional: a JSON summary of the whole run

The `serenity-json-summary-report` artifact writes one `serenity-summary.json` for the run. It is not enabled by default. Add it as a dependency of the Serenity Maven plugin and ask for the report:

```xml
<plugin>
  <groupId>net.serenity-bdd.maven.plugins</groupId>
  <artifactId>serenity-maven-plugin</artifactId>
  <version>${serenity.version}</version>
  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>net.serenity-bdd</groupId>
      <artifactId>serenity-json-summary-report</artifactId>
      <version>${serenity.version}</version>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>
  <!-- keep your existing executions -->
</plugin>
```

```bash
mvn serenity:reports -Dserenity.reports=json-summary
```

`serenity-summary.json` has `report`, `results` (`counts`: total, success, failure, error, pending, skipped ...; durations), `resultsByFeature` (each feature with its scenarios: `title`, `result` and for each outcome an `errorMessage`), `frequentFailures`, `unstableFeatures`, `coverage` and `tags`. It has the failure message of each scenario but not the failing step, the stack trace or the link to the outcome file, so for investigating a failure use the outcome files (or `results.py`). The goal ran after a failed build and produced it from the outcome files, with no HTML report.

## What this is not

- The outcome file format is Serenity's own. It is stable in practice but is not a published contract, so read the fields listed above and ignore the rest.
- The JUnit XML (`SERENITY-JUNIT-*.xml`) and Maven's `target/surefire-reports/*.xml` are the standard formats; use them when a tool expects JUnit XML.

## What an assistant should do after a run

1. Run the build (`mvn verify`). If it fails, do not stop at the console output.
2. Run `results.py` on `target/site/serenity`. Fix compile errors from the console first; they produce no outcome files.
3. For each failed test, read the message and the stack frame in your own code, and decide whether the test or the application is wrong. If the application is wrong, say so rather than editing the test to pass.
4. When all tests pass, build the report (`mvn verify` does it when the tests pass) and review it with `outline.py` and the review checklist.

<!-- https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_review_checklist -->

# Reviewing Tests and Living Documentation

Used by the `serenity-test-reviewer` agent after tests are written, and by anyone reviewing Serenity tests. Style-neutral: it applies to Page Objects, Screenplay and Cucumber, Selenium, Playwright and REST. Do not ask for a different style; judge the tests inside the style they use.

Read `living-documentation.md` first for what Serenity does with titles, steps and structure.

## What to look at

1. The test sources (and the feature files).
2. The report as a reader sees it: run the tests, then `python3 <skill>/scripts/outline.py <project>/target/site/serenity`. If the tests cannot run here, review the sources and say the report was not seen.
3. The task the user asked for, to check that the tests cover it.

## The checks

Each check is PASS, WEAK or FAIL. Quote the line or title, and write the replacement.

### A. Intent: does a reader learn the business rule?
- **A1** The scenario title states the rule or outcome in business words (not `testCheckout1`, not `shouldReturn201`, not a description of clicks).
- **A2** The scenario is about one behaviour. A title with "and" covering two rules should be two scenarios.
- **A3** It is clear why the behaviour matters or what the user gets (a title like "A reader sees an order number after paying" says it; "Checkout works" does not).
- **A4** Cucumber: the feature has a short business description; scenario outlines use meaningful example column names.

### B. Steps: business language
- **B1** Steps read as a narrated story with who/what, in the project's domain terms.
- **B2** No selectors, ids, URLs, sleeps, driver calls or HTTP codes in step text, titles or the test body (they belong inside page objects, tasks, step libraries, step definitions). In a REST test, a status code is fine inside the check, not as the step name.
- **B3** The final step/check states the business expectation ("the confirmation shows an order number"), and the check really proves that (see D1).
- **B4** One level of abstraction per scenario: business tasks at the top, mechanics inside them.

### C. Organisation: easy to navigate
- **C1** Scenarios are grouped by function (package/folder per capability, one class or feature file per feature, or `@Epic/@Feature/@Story`), not one big class and not by technical layer.
- **C2** The report tree (from `outline.py`) reads like a table of contents of what the application does. Names are business phrases, with no class name showing ("When signing in test": the class needs `@DisplayName`) and no duplicates.
- **C3** One grouping method for the whole project (not package structure mixed with `@Feature` annotations).
- **C4** Description files exist where an area needs explaining (Cucumber `readme.md`, or `src/test/resources/stories/<package path>/readme.md`) and are short and about the business.

### D. Test quality
- **D1** The assertions check what the title claims, with specific expected values from the task (not "page loaded", not `isNotNull`, not the same value read back from the test's own input). Ask: if the application broke in the way the title describes, would this test fail?
- **D2** No fixed sleeps. Waits are on a condition (Serenity waits, `WaitUntil`, Playwright auto-wait).
- **D3** Scenarios are independent: no shared mutable state between tests, no dependence on order, no static fields for scenario state.
- **D4** Test data is visible where it matters (the value a rule depends on is in the scenario, not hidden in a helper), and secrets are not hard-coded beyond what the task gave.
- **D5** No duplicated flows: repeated step sequences are a task, step method or Background.
- **D6** It follows the project's existing style, driver and runner, and does not mix styles in one test. The project builds and the tests were run or the reason is stated.
- **D7** Covers what was asked, including the negative case when the task mentioned one, and nothing invented beyond the application's described behaviour.

## Output

```
VERDICT: READY | NEEDS CHANGES

LIVING DOCUMENTATION AS A READER SEES IT
<the outline, trimmed>

FINDINGS (worst first)
1. [FAIL B2] src/test/java/.../CheckoutTest.java:31: step "Click #place-order" shows a selector
   Change to: Task.where("{0} places the order", ...)
...

WHAT IS GOOD
<one or two lines>
```

READY means no FAIL and at most two WEAK, and the report was seen. Be specific and brief: every finding says where it is and what to write instead. Do not edit files; the author applies the changes, and a second review follows if there were FAILs.
